translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 240.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 240.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十六】起強圉作噩，盡屠維大淵獻正月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 56] From Qiangyu Zuo'e through the first month of Tuwei Dayuanxian; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 56] From Qiangyu Zuo'e through the first month of Tuwei Dayuanxian—a span of slightly more than two years.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝中之下元和十二年（

translations.literal: Middle section, lower part, of the reign of Emperor Xianzong, the Illustrious, Cultured, Martial, Great, Sagely, and Divine Filial Emperor—Yuanhe year 12 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle section, lower part, of the reign of Emperor Xianzong—the Illustrious, Cultured, Martial, Great, Sagely, and Divine Filial Emperor—Yuanhe year 12 (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元八一七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, corresponding to the year 817 CE).
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, corresponding to the year 817 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，甲申，貶袁滋為撫州刺史。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on day jiashen, Yuan Zi was demoted and made prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the day jiashen, Yuan Zi was demoted to prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 李愬至唐州，軍中承喪敗之餘，士卒皆憚戰，愬知之。

translations.literal: When Li Su arrived at Tang Prefecture, the army was still in the aftermath of defeat and mourning, and the soldiers all feared battle; Su knew this.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Su reached Tang Prefecture, the army was still reeling from defeat, and every soldier dreaded fighting—Su understood this well.

sentences.zh: 有出迓者，愬謂之曰：「天子知愬柔懦，能忍恥，故使來拊循爾曹。

translations.literal: When men came out to meet him, Su said to them, "The Son of Heaven knows that Su is soft and cowardly and can endure disgrace, and therefore sent me to comfort and reassure you.
translations.idiomatic: When men came out to greet him, Su told them, "The Son of Heaven knows I am mild and timid, able to bear humiliation—that is why he sent me to comfort and reassure you.

sentences.zh: 至於戰攻進取，非吾事也。」

translations.literal: As for fighting, attacking, and advancing to seize ground—that is not my affair."
translations.idiomatic: As for fighting, storming positions, and driving forward—that is not my business."

sentences.zh: 眾信而安之。

translations.literal: The troops believed him and were reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The men believed him and settled down.

sentences.zh: 愬親行視，士卒傷病者存恤之，不事威嚴。

translations.literal: Su personally made the rounds; he cared for wounded and sick soldiers and did not put on a show of stern authority.
translations.idiomatic: Su went among the ranks himself, tending the wounded and sick, and made no display of harsh discipline.

sentences.zh: 或以軍政不肅為言，愬曰：「吾非不知也。

translations.literal: Some spoke of lax military discipline, and Su said, "It is not that I do not know.
translations.idiomatic: When some complained that military discipline was slack, Su said, "I am not unaware of that.

sentences.zh: 袁尚書專以恩惠懷賊，賊易之，聞吾至，必增備，故吾示之以不肅。

translations.literal: Minister Yuan relied solely on kindness to win over the rebels; the rebels looked down on him. When they hear I have come, they will surely heighten their guard, and therefore I show them laxity.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yuan tried to win the rebels over with kindness alone, and they took him lightly. When they hear I have arrived, they will certainly brace themselves—so I let them see slack discipline.

sentences.zh: 彼必以吾為懦而懈惰，然後可圖也。」

translations.literal: They will surely take me for a coward and grow slack; only then can we act."
translations.idiomatic: They are sure to think me timid and let their guard down—only then can we strike."

sentences.zh: 淮西人自以嘗敗高、袁二帥，輕愬名位素微，遂不為備。

translations.literal: The men of Huaixi, having themselves once defeated the two commanders Gao and Yuan, looked down on Su because his name and rank had always been slight, and therefore made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: The Huaixi rebels, having already routed commanders Gao and Yuan, despised Su for his modest rank and reputation—and so they took no precautions.

sentences.zh: 遣鹽鐵轉運副使程異督財賦於江、淮。

translations.literal: The Salt and Iron Transport Vice Commissioner Cheng Yi was sent to oversee revenues and levies on the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi, vice commissioner for salt and iron transport, was dispatched to supervise revenues along the Yangtze and Huai.

sentences.zh: 回鶻屢請尚公主，有司計其費近五百萬緡，時中原方用兵，故上未之許。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs repeatedly requested a princess in marriage; the relevant offices calculated the cost at nearly five million strings of cash. At that time the central plains were at war, and therefore the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs had repeatedly asked for an imperial princess; the ministries estimated the cost at nearly five million strings of cash. With the heartland still at war, the emperor held off granting the request.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯朔，遣回鶻摩尼僧等歸國，命宗正少卿李誠使回鶻諭意，以緩其期。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day xinmao, the Uyghur Manichaean monks and others were sent home; Director of the Imperial Clan Li Cheng was ordered as envoy to the Uyghurs to explain the court's intent and delay the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day xinmao, Uyghur Manichaean monks and others were sent home, and Li Cheng of the Imperial Clan Office was dispatched to the Uyghurs to explain the court's position and stall for time.

sentences.zh: 李愬謀襲蔡州，表請益兵，詔以昭義、河中、鄜坊步騎二千給之。

translations.literal: Li Su planned a surprise attack on Caizhou, memorialized requesting reinforcements, and was ordered two thousand infantry and cavalry from Zhaoyi, Hezhong, and Zhengfang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su planned a surprise strike on Caizhou and memorialized for more troops; the court ordered two thousand foot and horse from Zhaoyi, Hezhong, and Zhengfang sent to him.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，愬遣十將馬少良將十餘騎巡邏，遇吳元濟捉生虞候丁士良，與戰，擒之。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Su sent the Ten General Ma Shaoliang with a dozen-odd horsemen on patrol; they encountered Wu Yuanji's captive-taking inspector Ding Shiliang, fought, and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Su sent Ten General Ma Shaoliang with a little more than ten horsemen on patrol; they met Wu Yuanji's captive-taking inspector Ding Shiliang, fought him, and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 士良，元濟驍將，常為東邊患，眾請刳其心，愬許之。

translations.literal: Shiliang was a fierce general of Yuanji's and had long been a scourge on the eastern front; the troops asked to cut out his heart, and Su agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang was one of Yuanji's fiercest generals and had long terrorized the eastern front; the men demanded his heart cut out, and Su consented.

sentences.zh: 既而召詰之，士良無懼色。

translations.literal: Then he summoned and questioned him; Shiliang showed no fear.
translations.idiomatic: Su then summoned and questioned him; Shiliang showed not a trace of fear.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「真丈夫也！」

translations.literal: Su said, "A true man!
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "You are a true man!

sentences.zh: 命釋其縛。

translations.literal: He ordered his bonds removed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his bonds cut.

sentences.zh: 士良乃自言：「本非淮西士，貞元中隸安州，與吳氏戰，為其所擒，自分死矣。

translations.literal: Shiliang then spoke on his own: "I was not originally a man of Huaixi; in the Zhenyuan era I served An Prefecture, fought the Wu clan, was captured by them, and resigned myself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang then spoke freely: "I was never a native of Huaixi. In the Zhenyuan era I served An Prefecture, fought the Wu clan, was captured, and expected to die.

sentences.zh: 吳氏釋我而用之，我因吳氏而再生，故為吳氏父子竭力。

translations.literal: The Wu clan released me and employed me; through the Wu clan I lived again, and therefore I exerted myself for father and son Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu clan spared me and took me into their service; they gave me a second life, and so I gave father and son Wu my utmost.

sentences.zh: 昨日力屈，復為公所擒，亦分死矣。

translations.literal: Yesterday my strength failed and I was captured by you again; again I resign myself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday my strength gave out and you captured me again—I am ready to die once more.

sentences.zh: 今公又生之，請盡死以報德！」

translations.literal: Now you spare me again; I beg to give my life entirely to repay your kindness!"
translations.idiomatic: Now you spare me again—let me devote my life to repaying your grace!"

sentences.zh: 愬乃給其衣服器械，署為捉生將。

translations.literal: Su then supplied him with clothing and weapons and appointed him captive-taking commander.
translations.idiomatic: Su then gave him clothing and arms and appointed him commander of captive-taking.

sentences.zh: 己亥，淮西行營奏克蔡州古葛伯城。

translations.literal: On day jihai, the Huaixi campaign headquarters reported the capture of Gugebo City in Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, the Huaixi campaign headquarters reported the capture of Gugebo City in Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁士良言於李愬曰：「吳秀琳擁三千之眾，據文城柵，為賊左臂，官軍不敢近者，有陳光洽為之謀主也。

translations.literal: Ding Shiliang said to Li Su, "Wu Xiulin commands three thousand men and holds Wencheng palisade as the rebels' left arm; the reason government troops dare not approach is that Chen Guangqia serves as his strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Shiliang told Li Su, "Wu Xiulin holds three thousand men at Wencheng palisade—the rebels' left arm. Government troops dare not come near because Chen Guangqia is his strategist.

sentences.zh: 光洽勇而輕，好自出戰，請為公先擒光洽，則秀琳自降矣。」

translations.literal: Guangqia is brave but rash and likes to fight in person; allow me to seize Guangqia first for you, and Xiulin will surrender of himself."
translations.idiomatic: Guangqia is brave but reckless and likes to fight in person himself. Let me take Guangqia first, and Xiulin will surrender on his own."

sentences.zh: 戊申，士良擒光洽以歸。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Shiliang captured Guangqia and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Shiliang captured Guangqia and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 鄂岳觀察使李道古引兵出穆陵關。

translations.literal: E-Yue observation commissioner Li Daogu led troops out through Muling Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daogu, observation commissioner of E and Yue, led troops out through Muling Pass.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，攻申州，克其外郭，進攻子城。

translations.literal: On day jiayin, he attacked Shen Prefecture, took its outer wall, and pressed the attack on the inner citadel.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he attacked Shen Prefecture, took the outer wall, and pressed on against the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 城中守將夜出兵擊之，道古之眾驚亂，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: The garrison commander sent troops out by night to strike them; Daogu's force panicked and fell into disorder, and very many were killed.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison commander sallied by night; Daogu's troops panicked and broke, and a great many were killed.

sentences.zh: 道古，皋之子也。

translations.literal: Daogu was the son of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was the son of Li Gao.

sentences.zh: 淮西被兵數年，竭倉廩以奉戰士，民多無食，採菱芡魚鱉鳥獸食之，亦盡，相帥歸官軍者前後五千餘戶。

translations.literal: Huaixi had suffered warfare for years, exhausting its granaries to supply the warriors; many common people had no food and ate water chestnuts, gorgon fruit, fish, turtles, birds, and beasts until these too were gone; those who led one another back to the government army numbered more than five thousand households in all.
translations.idiomatic: Huaixi had been at war for years, draining its granaries to feed its soldiers. Many civilians went hungry, living on water chestnuts, gorgon nuts, fish, turtles, birds, and game until even those were exhausted. In waves, more than five thousand households made their way back to the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 賊亦患其耗糧食，不復禁。

translations.literal: The rebels also feared the drain on provisions and no longer forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, worried about the drain on their food supply, stopped trying to prevent it.

sentences.zh: 庚申，敕置行縣以處之，為擇縣令，使之撫養，並置兵以衛之。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, an edict established itinerant counties to settle them, selected county magistrates to nurture them, and also posted troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict established field counties to receive them, appointed magistrates to care for them, and stationed troops for their protection.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙丑，李愬自唐州徙屯宜陽柵。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day yichou, Li Su moved his encampment from Tang Prefecture to Yiyang palisade.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yichou, Li Su shifted his camp from Tang Prefecture to Yiyang palisade.

sentences.zh: 郗士美敗於柏鄉，拔營而歸，士卒死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Xi Shimei was defeated at Baixiang, struck camp and withdrew, and more than a thousand soldiers were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Shimei was defeated at Baixiang, broke camp and retreated, and lost more than a thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，賜程執恭名權。

translations.literal: On day wuchen, Cheng Zhigong was granted the personal name Quan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Cheng Zhigong was granted the personal name Quan.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，王承宗遣兵二萬入東光，斷白橋路。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Wang Chengzong sent twenty thousand troops into Dongguang and cut the Baiqiao road.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Wang Chengzong sent twenty thousand troops into Dongguang and severed the Baiqiao road.

sentences.zh: 程權不能御，以眾歸滄州。

translations.literal: Cheng Quan could not withstand them and led his force back to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Quan could not hold them off and withdrew with his troops to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 吳秀琳以文城柵降於李愬。

translations.literal: Wu Xiulin surrendered Wencheng palisade to Li Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xiulin surrendered Wencheng palisade to Li Su.

sentences.zh: 戊子，愬引兵至文城西五里，遣唐州刺史李進誠將甲士八千至城下，召秀琳，城中矢石如雨，眾不得前。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Su led troops to five li west of Wencheng, sent Tang Prefecture prefect Li Jincheng with eight thousand armored men to the foot of the wall, and summoned Xiulin; arrows and stones rained from the city like rain, and the force could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Su marched to a point five li west of Wencheng and sent Tang Prefecture prefect Li Jincheng with eight thousand armored men to the walls to summon Xiulin. Arrows and stones poured from the city like rain, and the troops could not advance.

sentences.zh: 進誠還報：「賊偽降，未可信也。」

translations.literal: Jincheng returned and reported, "The rebels are feigning surrender and cannot be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Jincheng returned and reported, "The rebels are feigning surrender—it cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「此待我至耳。」

translations.literal: Su said, "This is because they are waiting for me to arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "They are only waiting for me to arrive."

sentences.zh: 即前至城下，秀琳束兵投身馬足下，愬撫其背慰勞之，降其眾三千人。

translations.literal: He at once went forward to the foot of the wall; Xiulin bound up his weapons and threw himself at the foot of Su's horse; Su patted his back and comforted him, and accepted the surrender of his three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: He rode straight to the walls. Xiulin bound up his weapons and threw himself at the foot of Su's horse. Su patted his back and comforted him, and accepted the surrender of three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 秀琳將李憲有材勇，愬更其名曰忠義而用之，悉遷婦女於唐州，入據其城。

translations.literal: Xiulin's general Li Xian had talent and courage; Su changed his name to Zhongyi and employed him, moved all the women to Tang Prefecture, and entered to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin's general Li Xian was talented and brave; Su renamed him Zhongyi and put him to use, moved all the women to Tang Prefecture, and occupied the city.

sentences.zh: 於是唐、鄧軍氣復振，人有欲戰之志。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Tang and Deng armies' spirit revived, and men had the will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang and Deng armies' morale revived, and the men were eager to fight again.

sentences.zh: 賊中降者相繼於道，隨其所便而置之。

translations.literal: Surrenders from among the rebels followed one another on the road, and they were placed wherever convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel deserters came in one after another along the roads, and Su stationed them wherever it suited.

sentences.zh: 聞有父母者，給粟帛遣之，曰：「汝曹皆王人，勿棄親戚。」

translations.literal: When he heard any had parents, he gave grain and cloth and sent them off, saying, "You are all subjects of the king; do not abandon your kin."
translations.idiomatic: When he learned any had parents living, he gave them grain and cloth and sent them home, saying, "You are all the emperor's people—do not abandon your families."

sentences.zh: 眾皆感泣。

translations.literal: All were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: All were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 官軍與淮西兵夾殷水而軍，諸軍相顧望，無敢渡殷水者。

translations.literal: The government army and the Huaixi army encamped on opposite banks of the Yin River; the various armies looked at one another, and none dared cross the Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial and Huaixi forces faced each other across the Yin River; the various armies hung back, and none dared cross.

sentences.zh: 陳許兵馬使王沛先引兵五千渡涼水，據要地為城，於是河陽、宣武、河東、魏博等軍相繼皆度，進逼郾城。

translations.literal: Chen-Xu army horse commissioner Wang Pei first led five thousand men across the Liangshui, seized a strategic place and fortified it; thereupon the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Hedong, Weibo, and others crossed in succession and pressed toward Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pei, horse commissioner of Chen and Xu, first led five thousand men across the Liangshui and fortified a key position. Then the armies of Heyang, Xuanwu, Hedong, Weibo, and others crossed in turn and advanced on Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，李光顏敗淮西兵三萬於郾城，走其將張伯良，殺士卒什二三。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, Li Guangyan defeated thirty thousand Huaixi troops at Yancheng, put their general Zhang Boliang to flight, and killed one or two tenths of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Li Guangyan routed thirty thousand Huaixi troops at Yancheng, drove off their general Zhang Boliang, and killed perhaps a tenth or two of their men.

sentences.zh: 己丑，李愬遣山河十將董少玢等分兵攻諸柵。

translations.literal: On day jichou, Li Su sent the Ten Generals Dong Shaobin and others to divide forces and attack the various palisades.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou, Li Su sent the Ten Generals, including Dong Shaobin, to divide their forces and attack the various palisades.

sentences.zh: 其日，少玢下馬鞍山，拔路口柵。

translations.literal: That day Shaobin took Ma'anshan and captured Lukou palisade.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Shaobin took Ma'anshan and seized Lukou palisade.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，山河十將馬少良下碴岈山，擒淮西將柳子野。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on day xinmao, Ten General Ma Shaoliang took Chayashan and captured the Huaixi general Liu Ziye.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao, Ten General Ma Shaoliang took Chayashan and captured the Huaixi general Liu Ziye.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟以蔡人董昌齡為郾城令，質其母楊氏。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanji made the man of Cai Dong Changling magistrate of Yancheng and held his mother Lady Yang as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji appointed Dong Changling of Cai as magistrate of Yancheng and held his mother, Lady Yang, as hostage.

sentences.zh: 楊氏謂昌齡曰：「順死賢於逆生，汝去逆而吾死，乃孝子也；

translations.literal: Lady Yang said to Changling, "To die in obedience is nobler than to live in rebellion; if you leave the rebels and I die, you will be a filial son;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yang told Changling, "To die loyal is better than to live in rebellion. If you leave the rebels and I die, you will have acted as a filial son;

sentences.zh: 從逆而吾生，是戮吾也。」

translations.literal: if you follow the rebels and I live, that is to slaughter me."
translations.idiomatic: if you follow the rebels and I live, you will have killed me."

sentences.zh: 會官軍圍青陵，絕郾城歸路，郾城守將鄧懷金謀於昌齡，昌齡勸之歸國，懷金乃請降於李光顏曰：「城人之父母妻子皆在蔡州，請公來攻城，吾舉烽求救，救兵至，公逆擊之，蔡兵必敗，然後吾降，則父母妻子庶免矣。」

translations.literal: It happened that the government army besieged Qingling and cut Yancheng's route of return; Yancheng garrison commander Deng Huaijin consulted Changling, and Changling urged him to return to the state; Huaijin then asked to surrender to Li Guangyan, saying, "The people's parents, wives, and children are all in Caizhou; please come attack the city, and I will raise beacon fires to call for rescue; when the rescue force arrives, strike them in reverse—the Cai troops will surely be defeated—and then I will surrender, so that parents, wives, and children may be spared."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army besieged Qingling and cut off Yancheng's line of retreat, garrison commander Deng Huaijin consulted Changling, who urged him to rejoin the empire. Huaijin then offered to surrender to Li Guangyan, saying, "The townspeople's parents, wives, and children are all in Caizhou. Please attack the city, and I will raise beacon fires for help. When relief arrives, strike them from behind—the Cai troops will surely break—and then I will surrender, so our families may be spared."

sentences.zh: 光顏從之。

translations.literal: Guangyan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyan agreed.

sentences.zh: 乙未，昌齡、懷金舉城降，光顏引兵入據之。

translations.literal: On day yiwei, Changling and Huaijin surrendered the whole city; Guangyan led troops in to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Changling and Huaijin surrendered the entire city, and Guangyan marched in to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟聞郾城不守，甚懼。

translations.literal: When Wu Yuanji heard that Yancheng could not be held, he was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Yuanji learned Yancheng had fallen, he was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 時董重質將騾軍守洄曲，元濟悉發親近及守城卒詣重質以拒之。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Chongzhi commanded the mule army guarding Huaiqu; Yuanji sent out all his close followers and city garrison troops to Chongzhi to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi then held Huaiqu with the mule army; Yuanji sent out all his intimates and city garrison troops to Chongzhi to meet the threat.

sentences.zh: 李殷山河十將媯雅、田智榮下冶爐城。

translations.literal: Li Su ordered the Ten Generals Gui Ya and Tian Zhirong to take Yelü Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su ordered Ten Generals Gui Ya and Tian Zhirong to take Yelü Fort.

sentences.zh: 丙申，十將閻士榮下白狗、汶港二柵。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, Ten General Yan Shirong took the two palisades of Baigou and Wengang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Ten General Yan Shirong took the Baigou and Wengang palisades.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，媯雅、田智榮破西平。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Gui Ya and Tian Zhirong broke Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Gui Ya and Tian Zhirong stormed Xiping.

sentences.zh: 丙午，游弈兵馬使王義破楚城。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, roaming patrol horse commissioner Wang Yi took Chucheng.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, roaming patrol horse commissioner Wang Yi took Chucheng.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛酉，李愬遣柳子野、李忠義襲郎山，擒其守將梁希果。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day xinyou, Li Su sent Liu Ziye and Li Zhongyi to strike Langshan and captured its garrison commander Liang Xiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinyou, Li Su sent Liu Ziye and Li Zhongyi to raid Langshan and captured garrison commander Liang Xiguo.

sentences.zh: 六鎮討王承宗者兵十餘萬，迴環數千里，既無統帥，又相去運，期約難壹，由是歷二年無功，千里饋運，牛驢死者什四五。

translations.literal: The six circuits campaigning against Wang Chengzong had more than a hundred thousand troops encircling several thousand li; there was neither a supreme commander nor close coordination, and agreements were hard to unify; therefore for two years they achieved nothing, and on supply lines a thousand li long, one or four or five tenths of oxen and donkeys died.
translations.idiomatic: The six circuits campaigning against Wang Chengzong fielded more than a hundred thousand men spread across thousands of li. With no supreme commander and their camps far apart, they could not keep a single timetable—and so two years passed without success. On supply lines stretching a thousand li, perhaps forty or fifty percent of the draft animals died.

sentences.zh: 劉總既得武強，引兵出境才五里，留屯不進，月給度支錢十五萬緡。

translations.literal: After Liu Zong took Wuqiang, he led his army only five li beyond the border, then halted and did not advance, while receiving one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash per month from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Zong took Wuqiang, he marched only five li beyond the border, then halted and went no farther—while drawing one hundred fifty thousand strings of cash a month from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉及朝士多言「宜並力先取淮西。

translations.literal: Li Fengji and many court officials repeatedly said, "We should combine our strength and take Huaixi first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji and many at court kept saying, "We ought to concentrate our forces and take Huaixi first.

sentences.zh: 俟淮西平，乘其勝勢，回取恆冀，如拾芥耳！」

translations.literal: When Huaixi is pacified, riding the momentum of victory, we can turn and take Heng and Ji—it will be like picking up a mustard seed!"
translations.idiomatic: Once Huaixi is pacified, we can ride that victory to sweep up Heng and Ji—it will be as easy as picking up a mustard seed!"

sentences.zh: 上猶豫，久乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated and only after a long time agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated, but in time he agreed.

sentences.zh: 丙子，罷河北行營，各使還鎮。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, the Hebei campaign headquarters was abolished and each army was sent back to its circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the Hebei campaign headquarters was dissolved and each force sent back to its home circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，李愬遣方城鎮遏使李榮宗擊青喜城，拔之。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Li Su sent Fangcheng suppression commissioner Li Rongzong to attack Qingxi Fort and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Li Su sent Fangcheng suppression commissioner Li Rongzong against Qingxi Fort and took it.

sentences.zh: 愬每得降卒，必親引問委曲，由是賊中險易遠近虛實盡知之。

translations.literal: Whenever Su obtained surrendered soldiers, he personally questioned them in detail; thereby he came to know fully the rebels' strong and weak points, distances, and true and false conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Su took prisoners, he questioned them himself in detail—until he knew every strong point, weak point, distance, and ruse in the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 愬厚待吳秀琳，與之謀取蔡。

translations.literal: Su treated Wu Xiulin generously and plotted with him to take Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Su treated Wu Xiulin generously and plotted with him how to take Cai.

sentences.zh: 秀琳曰：「公欲取蔡，非得李祐不可，秀琳無能為也。」

translations.literal: Xiulin said, "If you wish to take Cai, you cannot do without Li You; Xiulin can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Xiulin said, "If you mean to take Cai, you cannot do it without Li You—I can do nothing for you there."

sentences.zh: 祐者，淮西騎將，有勇略，守興橋柵，常陵暴官軍。

translations.literal: You was a Huaixi cavalry general, brave and resourceful, who held Xingqiao palisade and often bullied the government army.
translations.idiomatic: You was a Huaixi cavalry commander—brave and shrewd—who held Xingqiao palisade and often ravaged the imperial forces.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，祐帥士卒刈麥於張柴村，愬召廂虞候史用誠，戒之曰：「爾以三百騎伏彼林中，又使人搖幟於前，若將焚其麥積者。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, You led soldiers to reap wheat at Zhangchai Village; Su summoned his adjutant Shi Yongcheng and instructed him, "Take three hundred horsemen and lie in ambush in that grove; also send men to wave banners in front as if about to burn their wheat stacks.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, You led his men to harvest wheat at Zhangchai Village. Su summoned adjutant Shi Yongcheng and instructed him, "Take three hundred horsemen and lie in the woods yonder. Send men to wave banners in front as if you mean to burn their wheat stacks.

sentences.zh: 祐素易官軍，必輕騎來逐之，爾乃發騎掩之，必擒之。」

translations.literal: You has always looked down on the government army and will surely come with light cavalry in pursuit; then launch your horsemen to envelop him—you will surely capture him."
translations.idiomatic: You has always despised the imperial army and will surely ride out lightly in pursuit. Then strike with your cavalry from cover—you are sure to take him."

sentences.zh: 用誠如言而往，生擒祐以歸。

translations.literal: Yongcheng went as instructed and captured You alive and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng did as he was told and brought You back alive.

sentences.zh: 將士以祐向日多殺官軍，爭請殺之。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers, because You had killed many government troops in the past, all asked to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and men, remembering how many imperial soldiers You had killed, clamored to put him to death.

sentences.zh: 愬不許，釋縛，待以客禮。

translations.literal: Su would not allow it, released his bonds, and treated him with the courtesy due a guest.
translations.idiomatic: Su refused, cut his bonds, and received him with the courtesy due a guest.

sentences.zh: 時愬欲襲蔡，而更密其謀，獨召祐及李忠義屏人語，或至夜分，他人莫得預聞。

translations.literal: At that time Su wished to strike Cai and kept his plan more secret; he summoned only You and Li Zhongyi to speak apart from others, sometimes until midnight, and no one else was allowed to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Su was planning a surprise on Cai and kept his design still more secret. He spoke with only You and Li Zhongyi behind closed doors, sometimes until midnight, and no one else was allowed to know.

sentences.zh: 諸將恐祐為變，多諫愬。

translations.literal: The generals feared You might turn traitor and many admonished Su.
translations.idiomatic: The generals feared You might turn on them and many urged Su against trusting him.

sentences.zh: 愬待祐益厚。

translations.literal: Su treated You all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Su treated You all the more generously.

sentences.zh: 士卒亦不悅，諸軍日有牒稱祐為賊內應，且言得賊謀者具言其事。

translations.literal: The soldiers were also displeased; day by day the armies sent memorials calling You a rebel agent within, and those who claimed to have captured rebel plans set forth the matter in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The rank and file were unhappy too; day after day the armies sent petitions calling You a rebel spy inside the camp, and men who claimed to have seized rebel plans laid out the case in detail.

sentences.zh: 愬恐謗先達於上，己不及救，乃持祐泣曰：「豈天不欲平此賊邪！

translations.literal: Su feared slander would reach the emperor first and he would be too late to save him; he took You by the hand and wept, saying, "Has Heaven no wish to pacify these rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Su feared the slander would reach the throne before he could act; he took You's hand and wept, saying, "Does Heaven not wish these rebels destroyed!

sentences.zh: 何吾二人相知之深而不能勝眾口也。」

translations.literal: Why, when you and I understand each other so deeply, can we not overcome the multitude of mouths!"
translations.idiomatic: Why, when you and I understand each other so well, can we not prevail against the crowd!"

sentences.zh: 因謂眾曰：「諸君既以祐為疑，請令歸死於天子。」

translations.literal: He then said to the troops, "Since you all suspect You, let him return to die before the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He then told the men, "Since you all suspect You, let him go back to answer for his life before the Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 乃械祐送京師，先密表其狀，且曰：「若殺祐，則無以成功。」

translations.literal: He then fettered You and sent him to the capital, first memorializing secretly on the situation and saying, "If You is killed, there will be no way to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: He had You shackled and sent to the capital, having first memorialized the emperor in secret, saying, "If You is killed, the campaign cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 詔釋之，以還愬。

translations.literal: An edict released him and returned him to Su.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him released and sent back to Su.

sentences.zh: 愬見之喜，執其手曰：「爾之得全，社稷之靈也！」

translations.literal: When Su saw him he was glad, took his hand, and said, "That you were spared is the blessing of the altars of state!"
translations.idiomatic: When Su saw him he rejoiced, took his hand, and said, "That you were spared is the blessing of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 乃署散兵馬使，令佩刀巡警，出入帳中。

translations.literal: He then appointed him irregular horse commissioner, ordered him to wear a sword on patrol, and allowed him to enter and leave the command tent.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed him irregular horse commissioner, armed him with a sword for patrol duty, and let him come and go in the command tent.

sentences.zh: 或與之同宿，密語不寐達曙，有竊聽於帳外者，但聞祐感泣聲。

translations.literal: Some lodged with him in the same tent; they spoke in secret without sleep until dawn; those who eavesdropped outside the tent heard only the sound of You weeping in emotion.
translations.idiomatic: Some shared his tent; he spoke with You in secret through the night until dawn. Men who listened outside heard only You weeping.

sentences.zh: 時唐、隨牙隊三千人，號六院兵馬，皆山南東道之精銳也。

translations.literal: At that time the Tang and Sui tooth corps of three thousand men, called the Six Courtyard horse and foot, were all elite troops of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang and Sui tooth corps of three thousand men—the Six Courtyard horse and foot—were the elite of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 愬又以祐為六院兵馬使。

translations.literal: Su also made You commissioner of the Six Courtyard horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Su also appointed You commissioner of the Six Courtyard horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 舊軍令，捨賊諜者屠其家。

translations.literal: By the old army regulation, anyone who harbored rebel spies had his household put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old army law, anyone who sheltered rebel spies had his entire household executed.

sentences.zh: 愬除其令，使厚待之。

translations.literal: Su abolished the regulation and had them treated generously.
translations.idiomatic: Su abolished that rule and ordered them treated generously instead.

sentences.zh: 諜反以情告愬，愬益知賊中虛實。

translations.literal: The spies in turn reported intelligence to Su, and Su came to know ever more fully the rebels' true and false conditions.
translations.idiomatic: The spies in turn brought Su intelligence, and he learned ever more of what was real and what was sham in the rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，愬遣兵攻朗山，淮西兵救之，官軍不利。

translations.literal: On day yiyou, Su sent troops to attack Langshan; Huaixi troops came to its relief, and the government army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Su sent troops against Langshan; Huaixi forces relieved it, and the imperial army was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 眾皆悵恨，愬獨歡然曰：「此吾計也！」

translations.literal: All were vexed and resentful, but Su alone said cheerfully, "This is my plan!
translations.idiomatic: The men were bitterly disappointed, but Su alone said cheerfully, "This is exactly what I intended!

sentences.zh: 乃募敢死士三千人，號曰突將，朝夕自教習之，使常為行備，欲以襲蔡。

translations.literal: He then recruited three thousand dare-to-die warriors, called them Shock Generals, and morning and evening drilled them himself, keeping them always ready on the march, intending to strike Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He then recruited three thousand dare-to-die warriors, called them Shock Generals, and drilled them morning and evening himself, keeping them ready to march—he meant to strike Cai.

sentences.zh: 會久雨，所在積水，未果。

translations.literal: It happened that long rains left standing water everywhere, and the plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: But prolonged rains left standing water everywhere, and the plan had to wait.

sentences.zh: 閏月，己亥，程異還自江、淮，得供軍錢百八十五萬緡。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day jihai, Cheng Yi returned from the Yangtze and Huai with one million eight hundred fifty thousand strings of cash for the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jihai, Cheng Yi returned from the Yangtze and Huai with one million eight hundred fifty thousand strings of cash for the army.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫韋綬兼太子侍讀，每以珍膳餉太子，又悅太子以諧謔。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and counsel grandee Wei Shou also served as the crown prince's reader; he often presented the prince with rare delicacies and also amused the prince with wit and banter.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shou, remonstrance and counsel grandee and reader to the crown prince, often sent the prince rare delicacies and amused him with wit and banter.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，丁未，罷綬侍讀，尋出為虔州刺史。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, on day dingwei he removed Shou as reader, and soon after sent him out as prefect of Qianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, on dingwei he removed Shou as reader and soon sent him out as prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 綬，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Shou was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was a native of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟見其下數叛，兵勢日蹙，六月，壬戌，上表謝罪，願束身自歸。

translations.literal: Wu Yuanji, seeing his subordinates repeatedly defect and his military position daily pressed, in the sixth month on day renxu memorialized begging pardon and offering to bind himself and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his men defect one after another and his position tighten daily, Wu Yuanji memorialized in the sixth month on renxu begging pardon and offering to surrender himself.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使賜詔，許以不死，而為左右及大將董重質所制，不得出。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy with an edict promising he would not be put to death, but he was controlled by his close attendants and the great general Dong Chongzhi and could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy with an edict promising his life, but his intimates and the great general Dong Chongzhi held him in check and he could not leave.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，大水，或平地二丈。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, great floods—in places two zhang deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, catastrophic floods—in places the water stood two zhang deep on level ground.

sentences.zh: 初，國子祭酒孔戣為華州刺史，明州歲貢蚶、蛤、淡菜，水陸遞夫勞費，戣奏疏罷之。

translations.literal: Earlier, director of the Imperial Academy Kong Kan, while prefect of Hua Prefecture, had memorialized to abolish Ming Prefecture's annual tribute of oysters, clams, and mussels, whose transport by land and water exhausted the relay laborers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Kong Kan of the Imperial Academy, while serving as prefect of Hua, had memorialized to end Ming Prefecture's annual tribute of oysters, clams, and mussels—the relay costs by land and water were ruinous.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，嶺南節度使崔詠薨，宰相奏擬代詠者數人，上皆不用，曰：「頃有諫進蚶、蛤、淡菜者為誰，可求其人與之。」

translations.literal: On day jiachen, Lingnan military governor Cui Yong died; the chief ministers memorialized several men to replace Yong, but the emperor used none of them and said, "Who was it that recently remonstrated against sending oysters, clams, and mussels? Find that man and give him the post."
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, Lingnan military governor Cui Yong died. The chief ministers proposed several successors, but the emperor rejected them all, saying, "Who was it that remonstrated against the oyster, clam, and mussel tribute? Find him and give him the post."

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以戣為嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: On day gengxu, Kan was made military governor of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Kan was appointed military governor of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍討淮西，四年不克，饋運疲弊，民至有以驢耕者。

translations.literal: The various armies campaigning against Huaixi had failed to conquer it in four years; supply transport was exhausted, and among the people some even plowed with donkeys.
translations.idiomatic: For four years the armies against Huaixi had failed to win; supply lines were exhausted, and peasants were reduced to plowing with donkeys.

sentences.zh: 上亦病之，以問宰相。

translations.literal: The emperor was also troubled by this and questioned the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was troubled too and asked his chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉等競言師老財竭，意欲罷兵。

translations.literal: Li Fengji and others all said the army was worn out and funds exhausted and wished to halt the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji and others argued that the army was exhausted and the treasury drained, and pressed to end the war.

sentences.zh: 裴度獨無言，上問之，對曰：「臣請自往督戰。」

translations.literal: Pei Du alone said nothing; the emperor asked him, and he replied, "Your servant asks to go in person to oversee the fighting."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du alone said nothing. When the emperor asked him, he replied, "I ask to go in person to oversee the fighting."

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上復謂度曰：「卿真能為朕行乎？」

translations.literal: On day yimao, the emperor again said to Du, "Can you truly go for me?"
translations.idiomatic: On yimao, the emperor asked Du again, "Can you truly go for me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣誓不與此賊俱生！

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant swears not to live together with these rebels!
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I swear I shall not live while these rebels live!

sentences.zh: 臣比觀吳元濟表，勢實窘蹙，但諸將心不壹，不並力迫之，故未降耳。

translations.literal: Your servant has lately observed Wu Yuanji's memorials—the situation is truly pressed and tight; only the generals' hearts are not united and they do not press him with combined force, and therefore he has not surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately read Wu Yuanji's memorials—he is truly cornered. Only the generals are not of one mind and do not press him together, and that is why he has not surrendered.

sentences.zh: 若臣自詣行營，諸將恐臣奪其功，必爭進破賊矣。」

translations.literal: If your servant goes in person to the campaign headquarters, the generals will fear I will seize their merit and will surely vie to advance and break the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: If I go to the front myself, the generals will fear I mean to steal their glory and will vie to smash the rebels."

sentences.zh: 上悅，丙戌，以度為門下侍郎、同平章事、兼彰義節度使，仍充淮西宣慰招討處置使。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased; on day bingxu, Du was made vice director of the Secretariat, fellow chief minister, and concurrent military governor of Zhangyi, and still appointed Huaixi pacification, campaign, and disposition commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased. On bingxu he made Du vice director of the Secretariat, chief minister, and concurrent Zhangyi military governor, and appointed him Huaixi pacification, campaign, and disposition commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又以戶部侍郎崔群為中書侍朗、同平章事。

translations.literal: Households vice minister Cui Qun was also made Secretariat attendant and fellow chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Households vice minister Cui Qun was also made Secretariat attendant and fellow chief minister.

sentences.zh: 制下，度以韓弘已為都統，不欲更為招討，請但稱宣慰處置使，仍奏刑部侍郎馬總為宣慰副使，右庶子韓愈為彰義行軍司馬，判官、書記皆朝廷之選，上皆從之。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Du, because Han Hong was already supreme commander, did not wish to be campaign commander as well and asked to be called only pacification and disposition commissioner; he also memorialized Punishments vice minister Ma Zong as pacification deputy commissioner, right censor's son Han Yu as Zhangyi campaign marshal, and chose court men for aides and secretaries—the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, Du noted that Han Hong was already supreme commander and asked to be styled only pacification and disposition commissioner. He memorialized Punishments vice minister Ma Zong as his deputy, right censor's son Han Yu as Zhangyi campaign marshal, and named court men as aides and secretaries—the emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 度將行，言於上曰：「臣若賊滅，則朝天有期；

translations.literal: As Du was about to depart, he said to the emperor, "If your servant destroys the rebels, then there will be a day to face Heaven again;
translations.idiomatic: As Du prepared to leave, he told the emperor, "If I destroy the rebels, I shall have a day to face you again;

sentences.zh: 賊在，則歸闕無日。」

translations.literal: while the rebels remain, there will be no day to return to the palace."
translations.idiomatic: while they remain, I shall never return to court."

sentences.zh: 上為之流涕。

translations.literal: The emperor wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚申，度赴淮西，上御通化門送之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day gengshen, Du went to Huaixi; the emperor rode out to Tonghua Gate to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengshen, Du set out for Huaixi; the emperor saw him off at Tonghua Gate.

sentences.zh: 右神武將軍張茂和，茂昭弟也，嘗以膽略自衒於度。

translations.literal: Right Divine Martial general Zhang Maohe, younger brother of Maozhao, had once boasted of his courage and stratagem to Du.
translations.idiomatic: Right Divine Martial general Zhang Maohe, younger brother of Maozhao, had once boasted to Du of his courage and skill.

sentences.zh: 度表為都押牙，茂和辭以疾，度奏請斬之。

translations.literal: Du memorialized to make him chief military aide; Maohe declined on grounds of illness, and Du memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized to make him chief military aide; Maohe pleaded illness, and Du memorialized asking that he be executed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此忠順之門，為卿遠貶。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is a house of loyalty and obedience; for your sake I will banish him far."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This is a loyal house—for your sake I will banish him far instead."

sentences.zh: 辛酉，貶茂和永州司馬。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Maohe was demoted to Yongzhou assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Maohe was demoted to assistant magistrate of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以嘉王傅高承簡為都押牙。

translations.literal: Prince of Jia tutor Gao Chengjian was made chief military aide.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jia tutor Gao Chengjian was made chief military aide.

sentences.zh: 承簡，崇文之子也。

translations.literal: Chengjian was the son of Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Chengjian was the son of Gao Chongwen.

sentences.zh: 李逢吉不欲討蔡，翰林學士令狐楚與逢吉善，度恐其合中外之勢以沮軍事，乃請改制書數字，且言其草制失辭。

translations.literal: Li Fengji did not wish to campaign against Cai; Hanlin academician Linghu Chu was on good terms with Fengji; Du feared they would combine court and field influence to obstruct the war effort and therefore asked to alter several characters in the edict and also said Chu's draft edict was faulty in wording.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji opposed the campaign against Cai; Hanlin academician Linghu Chu was his ally. Du feared they would combine court and field influence to obstruct the war and asked to alter several characters in the edict, charging that Chu's draft was faulty.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，罷楚為中書舍人。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Chu was removed to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Chu was demoted to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 李光顏、烏重胤與淮西戰，癸亥，敗於賈店。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin fought the Huaixi army; on day guihai they were defeated at Jiadian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan and Wu Chongyin fought the Huaixi army and on guihai were defeated at Jiadian.

sentences.zh: 裴度過襄城南白草原，淮西人以驍騎七百邀之。

translations.literal: As Pei Du passed the White Grass Plain south of Xiang Prefecture city, Huaixi men with seven hundred fierce horsemen waylaid him.
translations.idiomatic: As Pei Du crossed the White Grass Plain south of Xiangcheng, seven hundred Huaixi horsemen ambushed him.

sentences.zh: 鎮將楚丘曹華知而為備，擊卻之。

translations.literal: Garrison commander Cao Hua of Chuqiu learned of it and made preparations, struck them, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Cao Hua of Chuqiu learned of it, made ready, struck them, and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 度雖辭招討名，實行無帥事，以郾城為治所。

translations.literal: Although Du declined the title of campaign commander, in practice he performed the duties of a commander-in-chief and made Yancheng his seat of government.
translations.idiomatic: Though Du had declined the title of campaign commander, in practice he commanded as supreme general and made Yancheng his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 甲申，至郾城。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, he reached Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he reached Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，諸道皆有中使監陳，進退不由主將，勝則先使獻捷，不利則陵挫百端。

translations.literal: Earlier, every circuit had palace envoys supervising the encampments; advance and retreat did not depend on the commanding generals; if victorious the envoys first reported the triumph, if things went badly they heaped a hundred abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, every circuit had palace eunuchs supervising the camps; generals could not command advance or retreat. If victorious, the eunuchs reported the triumph first; if not, they heaped abuse on every side.

sentences.zh: 度悉奏去之，諸將始得專軍事，戰多有功。

translations.literal: Du memorialized to remove them all; the generals were then able to command military affairs exclusively, and in battle they often achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Du memorialized to remove them all; only then could the generals command their own troops, and battles began to go well.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚子，淮西兵寇殷水鎮，殺三將，焚芻蒿而去。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day gengzi, Huaixi troops raided Yinshui post, killed three generals, burned fodder and thatch, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengzi, Huaixi troops raided Yinshui post, killed three generals, burned fodder and thatch, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，上為廣陵王，布衣張宿以辯口得幸。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was Prince of Guangling, the commoner Zhang Su won favor through eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was still Prince of Guangling, a commoner named Zhang Su won favor through his eloquence.

sentences.zh: 及即位，累官至比部員外郎。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Su rose in office to outer court director of the Justice Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: After his accession, Su rose to outer court director of the Justice Ministry.

sentences.zh: 宿招權受賂於外，門下侍郎、同平章事李逢吉惡之。

translations.literal: Su traded on power and accepted bribes outside the court; vice director of the Secretariat and fellow chief minister Li Fengji hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Su traded on his influence and took bribes; vice director Li Fengji hated him.

sentences.zh: 上欲以宿為諫議大夫，逢吉曰：「諫議重任，必能可否朝政，始宜為之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Su remonstrance and counsel grandee; Fengji said, "That office is a weighty charge; one must be able to approve or reject court policy—only then is he fit for it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make Su remonstrance and counsel grandee. Fengji said, "That office is a weighty charge—one must be able to approve or reject court policy. Only then is he fit.

sentences.zh: 宿小人，豈得竊賢者之位！

translations.literal: Su is a petty man—how can he usurp the place of the worthy!
translations.idiomatic: Su is a petty man—how can he steal the place of the worthy!

sentences.zh: 必欲用宿，請先去臣乃可。」

translations.literal: If you must use Su, please remove me first—only then will it do."
translations.idiomatic: If you must use Su, remove me first—only then will it do."

sentences.zh: 上由是不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 逢吉又與裴度異議，上方倚度以平蔡。

translations.literal: Fengji also differed in opinion from Pei Du, while the emperor was relying on Du to pacify Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji also clashed with Pei Du, while the emperor was relying on Du to pacify Cai.

sentences.zh: 丁未，罷逢吉為東川節度使。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Fengji was removed to military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Fengji was sent out as military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，李愬將攻吳房，諸將曰：「今日往亡。」

translations.literal: On day jiayin, Li Su was about to attack Wufang; the generals said, "Today is a day of going-forth-and-death."
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Li Su prepared to attack Wufang; the generals said, "Today is an ill-omened day for marching."

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「吾兵少，不足戰，宜出其不意。

translations.literal: Su said, "Our troops are few and not enough to fight; we should strike where they do not expect us.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Our force is too small to fight a straight battle—we must take them by surprise.

sentences.zh: 彼以往亡不吾虞，正可擊也。」

translations.literal: They, because it is a going-forth-and-death day, will not guard against us—we can strike."
translations.idiomatic: They will think us deterred by the ill omen and let our guard down—that is when we strike."

sentences.zh: 遂往，克其外城，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: He then went, took the outer wall, and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He marched, took the outer wall, and cut off more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 餘眾保子城，不敢出。

translations.literal: The remaining force held the inner citadel and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors held the inner citadel and dared not come out.

sentences.zh: 愬引兵還以誘之，淮西將孫獻忠果以驍騎五百追擊其背。

translations.literal: Su withdrew his troops to lure them; the Huaixi general Sun Xianzhong indeed came with five hundred fierce horsemen to strike their rear.
translations.idiomatic: Su withdrew to lure them out; Huaixi general Sun Xianzhong indeed came with five hundred horsemen to strike their rear.

sentences.zh: 眾驚，將走，愬下馬據胡床，令曰：「敢退者斬！」

translations.literal: The troops were alarmed and about to flee; Su dismounted, sat on a camp chair, and ordered, "Whoever dares retreat—beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: The men panicked and started to flee; Su dismounted, sat on a camp chair, and ordered, "Anyone who retreats—beheaded!"

sentences.zh: 返旆力戰，獻忠死，淮西兵乃退。

translations.literal: They turned their banners and fought with all their strength; Xianzhong was killed, and the Huaixi troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: They wheeled about and fought with all their strength; Xianzhong was killed, and the Huaixi force withdrew.

sentences.zh: 或勸愬乘勝攻其子城，可拔也。

translations.literal: Some urged Su to press the victory and attack the inner citadel—it could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Su to press on and take the inner citadel while he could.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「非吾計也。」

translations.literal: Su said, "That is not my plan."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "That is not my plan."

sentences.zh: 引兵還營。

translations.literal: He led the troops back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: He led the troops back to camp.

sentences.zh: 李祐言於李愬曰：「蔡之精兵皆在洄曲，及四境拒守，守州城者皆羸老之卒，可以乘虛直抵其城。

translations.literal: Li You said to Li Su, "Cai's elite troops are all at Huaiqu and guarding the four borders; those who hold the prefectural city are all weak and old soldiers—you can exploit the void and strike straight at the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li You told Li Su, "Cai's best troops are all at Huaiqu and on the borders; only weak and old men hold the city. You can strike through the gap straight at Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 比賊將聞之，元濟已成擒矣。」

translations.literal: By the time the rebel generals hear of it, Yuanji will already be captured."
translations.idiomatic: By the time their generals hear of it, Yuanji will already be your prisoner."

sentences.zh: 愬然之。

translations.literal: Su approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Su agreed.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，甲子，遣掌書記鄭澥至郾城，密白裴度。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day jiazi, he sent chief secretary Zheng Xie to Yancheng to report secretly to Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiazi, he sent chief secretary Zheng Xie to Yancheng to brief Pei Du in secret.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「兵非出奇不勝，常侍良圖也。」

translations.literal: Du said, "In war, without the unexpected there is no victory—this is an excellent plan, Vice Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Du said, "In war, only the unexpected wins—this is an excellent plan, Vice Censor."

sentences.zh: 上竟用張宿為諫議大夫，崔群、王涯固諫，不聽；

translations.literal: The emperor in the end made Zhang Su remonstrance and counsel grandee; Cui Qun and Wang Ya firmly remonstrated, but he would not listen;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor went ahead and made Zhang Su remonstrance and counsel grandee; Cui Qun and Wang Ya remonstrated firmly, but he would not listen;

sentences.zh: 乃請以為權知諫議大夫，許之。

translations.literal: they then asked that he be made acting remonstrance and counsel grandee, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: they then asked that he be made acting remonstrance and counsel grandee, and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 宿由是怨執政及當時端方之士，與皇甫鎛相表裡，譖去之。

translations.literal: Su therefore resented the chief ministers and the upright men of the time; he worked inside and out with Huangfu Bo and slandered them until they were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Su therefore resented the chief ministers and the upright men of the day; he worked hand in glove with Huangfu Bo to slander them out of office.

sentences.zh: 裴度帥僚佐觀築城於沱口，董重質帥騎出五溝，邀之，大呼而進，注弩挺刃，勢將及度。

translations.literal: Pei Du led his staff to observe fortification work at Tuokou; Dong Chongzhi led horsemen out from Wugou to waylay them, shouting as they advanced, nocking crossbows and drawing blades, their momentum about to reach Du.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du led his staff to inspect fortifications at Tuokou; Dong Chongzhi led cavalry out from Wugou to ambush them, shouting as they charged with crossbows drawn and blades ready, nearly upon Du.

sentences.zh: 李光顏與田布力戰，拒之，度僅得入城。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan and Tian Bu fought with all their strength and held them off; Du barely got inside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan and Tian Bu fought them off with all their strength; Du barely made it inside the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊退，布扼其溝中歸路。

translations.literal: When the rebels withdrew, Bu blocked their return route in the ditch.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels withdrew, Bu blocked their escape route through the ditch.

sentences.zh: 賊下馬逾溝，墜壓死者千餘人。

translations.literal: The rebels dismounted to cross the ditch; more than a thousand were killed in falls and crushing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels dismounted to cross the ditch; more than a thousand were killed in the crush.

sentences.zh: 辛未，李愬命馬步都虞候、隨州刺史史旻等留鎮文城，命李祐、李忠義帥突將三千為前驅，自與監軍將三千人為中軍，命李進誠將三千人殿其後。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, Li Su ordered horse and foot chief adjutant and Sui Prefecture prefect Shi Min and others to remain and garrison Wencheng; ordered Li You and Li Zhongyi to lead three thousand Shock Generals as vanguard; himself with the army supervisor led three thousand men as center army; ordered Li Jincheng to lead three thousand men as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Li Su left horse and foot chief adjutant Shi Min, prefect of Sui, and others to garrison Wencheng; ordered Li You and Li Zhongyi to lead three thousand Shock Generals as vanguard; himself with the army supervisor led three thousand as the center; and ordered Li Jincheng with three thousand to bring up the rear.

sentences.zh: 軍出，不知所之。

translations.literal: When the army set out, no one knew where it was going.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched out, no one knew where it was bound.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「但東行。」

translations.literal: Su said, "Simply march east."
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Simply march east."

sentences.zh: 行六十里，夜，至張柴村，盡殺其戍卒及烽子。

translations.literal: They marched sixty li; at night they reached Zhangchai Village, killed all its garrison troops and beacon guards.
translations.idiomatic: They marched sixty li and by night reached Zhangchai Village, where they killed every garrison soldier and beacon guard.

sentences.zh: 據其柵，命士卒少休，食干□，整羈靮，留義成軍五百人鎮之，以斷朗山救兵。

translations.literal: They seized its palisade, ordered the soldiers a brief rest, ate dry provisions, readied bridles and reins, left five hundred Yicheng troops to garrison it and cut off Langshan relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the palisade, let the men rest briefly, ate dry rations, tightened saddles and bridles, left five hundred Yicheng troops to hold it and block relief from Langshan.

sentences.zh: 命丁士良將五百人斷洄曲及諸道橋樑，復夜引兵出門。

translations.literal: He ordered Ding Shiliang with five hundred men to sever Huaiqu and the bridges on the various roads, then again led troops out by night through the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Ding Shiliang with five hundred men to cut Huaiqu and the bridges on every road, then led his army out through the gate again by night.

sentences.zh: 諸將請所之，愬曰：「入蔡州取吳元濟！」

translations.literal: The generals asked where they were going; Su said, "Into Caizhou to take Wu Yuanji!"
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked where they were going. Su said, "Into Caizhou to take Wu Yuanji!"

sentences.zh: 諸將皆失色。

translations.literal: All the generals turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Every general turned pale.

sentences.zh: 監軍哭曰：「果落李祐奸計！」

translations.literal: The army supervisor wept and said, "We have truly fallen into Li You's treacherous plot!"
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor wept, "We have truly fallen into Li You's treacherous plot!"

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，旌旗裂，人馬凍死者相望。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; banners and flags tore; men and horses who froze to death lined the route.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard raged; banners tore in the wind; frozen men and horses lined the road.

sentences.zh: 天陰黑，自張柴村以東道路，皆官軍所未嘗行，人人自以為必死，然畏愬，莫敢違。

translations.literal: The sky was dark; from Zhangchai Village eastward the roads were all paths the government army had never traveled; every man thought he would surely die, yet they feared Su and none dared disobey.
translations.idiomatic: The sky was black; east of Zhangchai every road was one the imperial army had never taken. Every man thought he was marching to his death, yet they feared Su and none dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 夜半，雪愈甚，行七十里，至州城。

translations.literal: At midnight the snow grew heavier; they marched seventy li and reached the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the snow grew heavier; they marched seventy li and reached the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 近城有鵝鴨池，愬令驚之以混軍聲。

translations.literal: Near the city was a pool of geese and ducks; Su ordered them startled to muffle the sound of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Near the walls was a goose and duck pond; Su had them startled so their clamor would cover the army's noise.

sentences.zh: 自吳少誠拒命，官軍不至蔡州城下三十餘年，故蔡人不為備。

translations.literal: Since Wu Shaocheng defied orders, government troops had not come beneath the walls of Caizhou for more than thirty years, and therefore the people of Cai made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wu Shaocheng's rebellion, imperial troops had not come beneath Caizhou's walls in more than thirty years, and the people of Cai were unprepared.

sentences.zh: 壬申，四鼓，愬至城下，無一人知者。

translations.literal: On day renshen, at the fourth watch, Su reached the foot of the wall, and not a soul knew.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, at the fourth watch, Su reached the foot of the wall—and not a soul knew.

sentences.zh: 李愬、李忠義钁其城為坎以先登，壯士從之。

translations.literal: Li Su and Li Zhongyi dug the wall into steps with picks and climbed first; stalwart men followed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su and Li Zhongyi dug footholds in the wall with picks and went up first; the bravest men followed.

sentences.zh: 守門卒方熟寐，盡殺之，而留擊柝者，使擊柝如故，遂開門納眾。

translations.literal: The gate guards were just in deep sleep; they killed them all, but kept the night-watch striker, making him strike the clapper as before, then opened the gate and admitted the host.
translations.idiomatic: The gate guards were fast asleep. Su's men killed them all but spared the watchman who beat the night clapper, making him continue as before, then opened the gate and let the army in.

sentences.zh: 及裡城，亦然，城中皆不之覺。

translations.literal: Reaching the inner wall, likewise—they did the same—and throughout the city none noticed.
translations.idiomatic: At the inner wall they did the same; no one in the city noticed.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴，雪止，愬入居元濟外宅。

translations.literal: At cockcrow the snow ceased; Su entered and took up residence in Yuanji's outer residence.
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow the snow stopped. Su entered and occupied Wu Yuanji's outer residence.

sentences.zh: 或告元濟曰：「官軍至矣！」

translations.literal: Someone reported to Yuanji, saying, "The government army has arrived!
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Wu Yuanji, "The imperial army is here!

sentences.zh: 元濟尚寢，笑曰：「俘囚為盜耳！

translations.literal: Yuanji was still abed and laughed, saying, "Captives turned robbers, that is all!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji was still in bed and laughed, "Just some prisoners turned raiders!

sentences.zh: 曉當盡戮之。」

translations.literal: At dawn they shall be wholly slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn we'll slaughter them all.

sentences.zh: 又有告者曰：「城陷矣！」

translations.literal: Another reporter said, "The city has fallen!
translations.idiomatic: Another messenger cried, "The city has fallen!

sentences.zh: 元濟曰：「此必洄曲子弟就吾求寒衣也。」

translations.literal: Yuanji said, "This must be the youths of Huaiqu coming to me to beg for winter garments.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji said, "It must be men from Huaiqu coming to ask for winter clothes.

sentences.zh: 起，聽於廷，聞愬軍號令曰：「常侍傳語！」

translations.literal: He rose and listened in the court, hearing Su's army orders: "The Vice Censor-in-Chief conveys a message!
translations.idiomatic: He got up and listened in the courtyard, hearing Su's troops shout, "The Imperial Commissioner sends word!

sentences.zh: 應者近萬人。

translations.literal: Those who answered were nearly ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten thousand voices answered.

sentences.zh: 元濟始懼，曰：「何等常侍，能至於此！」

translations.literal: Yuanji at last grew afraid and said, "What sort of Vice Censor-in-Chief could come to this!
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji finally panicked. "What kind of commissioner reaches this far!

sentences.zh: 乃帥左右登牙城拒戰。

translations.literal: He then led his attendants up to the citadel wall to resist in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He led his personal guard up to the citadel to fight.

sentences.zh: 時董重質擁精兵萬餘人據洄曲。

translations.literal: At that time Dong Chongzhi held more than ten thousand elite troops occupying Huaiqu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi held Huaiqu with more than ten thousand crack troops.

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「元濟所望者，重質之救耳。」

translations.literal: Su said, "What Yuanji hopes for is only Chongzhi's rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "All Wu Yuanji is waiting for is a rescue from Dong Chongzhi.

sentences.zh: 乃訪重質家，厚撫之，遣其子傳道持書諭重質。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sought out Chongzhi's family, treated them generously, and sent his son Chuandao bearing a letter to persuade Chongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Su found Chongzhi's family, treated them kindly, and sent Chongzhi's son Chuandao with a letter to win him over.

sentences.zh: 重質遂單騎詣愬降。

translations.literal: Chongzhi thereupon came alone on horseback to Su and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi rode to Su alone and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 愬遣李進誠攻牙城，毀其外門，得甲庫，取其器械。

translations.literal: Su sent Li Jincheng to attack the citadel, destroyed its outer gate, seized the armory, and took its weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Su sent Li Jincheng to assault the citadel, smashed its outer gate, captured the armory, and seized its weapons.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，復攻之，燒其南門，民爭負薪芻助之，城上矢如□胃毛。

translations.literal: On day guiyou they attacked again, burned the south gate; the people scrambled to carry firewood and fodder to help; on the wall arrows were thick as □ hedgehog bristles.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou they attacked again and burned the south gate. Civilians rushed to bring firewood and fodder to help. On the walls arrows stood thick as hedgehog quills.

sentences.zh: 晡時，門壞，元濟於城上請罪，進誠梯而下之。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon the gate was broken; Yuanji on the wall pleaded guilty; Jincheng brought him down by ladder.
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the gate gave way. Wu Yuanji surrendered from the wall, and Li Jincheng brought him down on a ladder.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，愬以檻車送元濟詣京師，且告於裴度。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu Su sent Yuanji to the capital in a caged cart and also reported to Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Su sent Wu Yuanji to the capital in a prison cart and notified Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 是日，申、光二州及諸鎮兵二萬餘人相繼來降。

translations.literal: That day more than twenty thousand troops of Shen and Guang prefectures and the various garrisons came to surrender in succession.
translations.idiomatic: That same day more than twenty thousand soldiers from Shen and Guang and the allied garrisons surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 自元濟就擒，愬不戮一人，凡元濟官吏、帳下、廚廄之卒，皆復其職，使之不疑，然後屯於鞠場以待裴度。

translations.literal: From the time Yuanji was captured, Su put none to death; all Yuanji's officials, retainers, and kitchen and stable troops he restored to their posts so they would not doubt him, then encamped at the drill ground to await Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Yuanji was taken, Su executed no one. He restored all of Yuanji's officials, staff, and stable and kitchen guards to their posts to keep them at ease, then camped at the drill field to await Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 以淮南節度使李鄘為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Li Yong, Military Governor of Huainan, was made Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Councilor of State.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong, governor of Huainan, was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Associate Chief Councilor.

sentences.zh: 己卯，淮西行營奏獲吳元濟，光祿少卿楊元卿言於上曰：「淮西大有珍寶，臣能知之，往取必得。」

translations.literal: On day jimao the Huaixi campaign headquarters reported the capture of Wu Yuanji; Palace Officer Yang Yuanqing said to the emperor, "Huaixi holds great treasures; your servant can locate them—a visit will surely obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the Huaixi headquarters reported Wu Yuanji's capture. Palace Officer Yang Yuanqing told the emperor, "Huaixi holds great treasures. I know where they are and can fetch them for you.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕討淮西，為人除害，珍寶非所求也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "We raised the campaign against Huaixi to remove harm for the people; treasures are not what We seek.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I sent this campaign against Huaixi to rid the realm of a scourge. I did not come for treasure.

sentences.zh: 董重質之去洄曲軍也，李光顏馳入其壁，悉降其眾。

translations.literal: When Dong Chongzhi left the Huaiqu army, Li Guangyan galloped into its encampment and wholly accepted the surrender of its host.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Chongzhi left Huaiqu, Li Guangyan rode into the camp and accepted the surrender of his entire force.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，裴度遣馬總先入蔡州慰撫。

translations.literal: On day gengchen Pei Du sent Ma Zong ahead into Caizhou to comfort and reassure.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen Pei Du sent Ma Zong ahead into Caizhou to pacify the city.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，度建彰義軍節，將降卒萬餘人入城，李愬具橐鞬出迎，拜於路左。

translations.literal: On day xinsi Du established the Zhangyi command; leading more than ten thousand surrendered troops into the city, Li Su fully equipped saddle and bridle and came out to meet him, bowing at the left of the road.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Pei Du entered as Military Commissioner of Zhangyi with more than ten thousand surrendered troops. Li Su came out in full armor to meet him and bowed by the roadside.

sentences.zh: 度將避之，愬曰：「蔡人頑悖，不識上下之分，數十年矣。

translations.literal: Du was about to avoid this; Su said, "The people of Cai are stubborn and rebellious and know not the distinction of high and low—it has been decades.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du tried to decline. Su said, "The people of Cai have been stubborn and defiant for decades. They no longer know their place.

sentences.zh: 願公因而示之，使知朝廷之尊。」

translations.literal: I wish you would take this occasion to show them, so they may know the honor of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Please accept this so they may see the dignity of the throne.

sentences.zh: 度乃受之。

translations.literal: Du thereupon accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du then accepted the salute.

sentences.zh: 李愬還軍文城，諸將請曰：「始公敗於郎山而不憂，勝於吳房而不取，冒大風甚雪而不止，孤軍深入而不懼，然卒以成功，皆眾人所不諭也，敢問其故？」

translations.literal: Li Su returned the army to Wencheng; the generals requested, saying, "At the start you were defeated at Langshan yet were not troubled; victorious at Wufang yet did not take it; braved great wind and heavy snow without stopping; advanced deep alone without fear—yet in the end succeeded. These are all things the host did not understand; we dare ask the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Back at Wencheng the generals asked Li Su, "You were routed at Langshan yet showed no concern; you beat the enemy at Wufang yet did not take the town; you marched through blizzard and gale without halting; you led a lone army deep into enemy country without fear—and still you won. None of us understood. What was your reasoning?

sentences.zh: 愬曰：「朗山不利，則賊輕我而不為備矣。

translations.literal: Su said, "Langshan going badly meant the rebels would slight us and make no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "Defeat at Langshan made the rebels despise us and let their guard down.

sentences.zh: 取吳房，則其眾奔蔡，並力固守，故存之以分其兵。

translations.literal: Taking Wufang would send its troops fleeing to Cai to unite in strength and hold fast; therefore we kept it to divide their forces.
translations.idiomatic: If we had taken Wufang, its garrison would have fled to Caizhou and united for a stronger defense. I held Wufang to split their strength.

sentences.zh: 風雪陰晦，則烽火不接，不知吾至。

translations.literal: Wind and snow with overcast sky meant beacon fires could not connect—they would not know we had arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The blizzard and darkness broke the beacon chain, so they never knew we were coming.

sentences.zh: 孤軍深入，則入皆致死，戰自倍矣。

translations.literal: A lone army advancing deep meant every man would fight to the death, and battle strength would of itself double.
translations.idiomatic: A lone army far from home fights as if there is no retreat—every man's strength doubles.

sentences.zh: 夫視元者不顧近，慮大者不計細，若矜小勝，恤小敗，先自撓矣，何暇立功乎！」

translations.literal: One who fixes his gaze on the origin does not attend to what is near; one who considers what is large does not reckon small matters. If one prides himself on small victories and pities small defeats, he first undermines himself—whence leisure to achieve merit!
translations.idiomatic: Who aims at the distant goal ignores the near setback; who thinks in grand terms does not count petty losses. Fuss over small wins and small defeats and you defeat yourself—what time is left to win the war!

sentences.zh: 眾皆服。

translations.literal: The host all submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were convinced.

sentences.zh: 愬儉於奉己而豐於待士，知賢不疑，見可能斷，此其所以成功也。

translations.literal: Su was sparing toward himself and generous in treating officers; he knew the worthy and trusted them without suspicion; seeing what could be done he decided—this was how he succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Su lived sparingly but treated his officers generously. He recognized talent and trusted it without hesitation; when he saw an opening he acted. That is why he won.

sentences.zh: 裴度以蔡卒為牙兵，或諫曰：「蔡人反仄者尚多，不可不備。」

translations.literal: Pei Du took Cai troops as his personal guard; someone remonstrated, saying, "Many among the people of Cai remain restless in rebellion; one cannot but take precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du made surrendered Caizhou troops his personal guard. Someone warned him, "Many in Cai remain unreconciled. You must stay on guard.

sentences.zh: 度笑曰：「吾為彰義節度使，元惡既擒，蔡人則吾人也，又何疑焉！」

translations.literal: Du laughed and said, "I am Military Commissioner of Zhangyi; the chief villain is already captured—the people of Cai are then Our people; why any doubt!
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du laughed. "I am governor of Zhangyi now. With the ringleader captured, the people of Cai are my people. Why should I doubt them?

sentences.zh: 蔡人聞之感泣。

translations.literal: The people of Cai, hearing this, were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Cai heard this, many wept.

sentences.zh: 先是吳氏父子阻兵，禁人偶語於塗，夜不然燭，有以酒食相過從者罪死。

translations.literal: Earlier the Wu father and son obstructed with arms; they forbade people to speak in pairs on the road, at night to light candles; those who visited one another with wine and food were punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Wu father and son, soldiers blocked the roads. Speaking in pairs on the street was forbidden. Candles at night were banned. Anyone who shared food or drink with a neighbor faced death.

sentences.zh: 度既視事，下令惟禁盜賊鬥殺，餘皆不問，往來者不限晝夜，蔡人始知有生民之樂。

translations.literal: Once Du assumed office he issued orders forbidding only thieving, brawling, and killing; everything else was not inquired into; comings and goings were not restricted day or night—the people of Cai first knew the joy of being alive.
translations.idiomatic: Once Pei Du took office he outlawed only theft, brawling, and murder. Everything else was permitted. People could come and go at any hour. For the first time the people of Cai knew what it meant to live as free subjects.

sentences.zh: 甲申，詔韓弘、裴度條列平蔡將士功狀及蔡之將士降者，皆差第以聞。

translations.literal: On day jiashen an edict ordered Han Hong and Pei Du to itemize the merit records of the generals and troops who pacified Cai and the surrendered generals and troops of Cai, all ranked in grades and reported.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the throne ordered Han Hong and Pei Du to rank the achievements of all who had helped pacify Cai and all who had surrendered from Cai, and report the list.

sentences.zh: 淮西州縣百姓，給復二年；

translations.literal: The common people of Huaixi prefectures and counties: tax relief for two years;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Huaixi prefectures and counties were granted two years of tax exemption;

sentences.zh: 近賊四州，免來年夏稅。

translations.literal: The four prefectures near the rebels: next year's summer tax remitted.
translations.idiomatic: the four frontier prefectures nearest the rebels were exempted from the next summer's tax levy.

sentences.zh: 官軍戰亡者，皆為收葬，給其家衣糧五年；

translations.literal: Those of the government army who died in battle—all were gathered for burial; their families given clothing and grain for five years;
translations.idiomatic: Every soldier who fell in battle was buried at public expense; families received rations and clothing for five years;

sentences.zh: 其因戰傷殘廢者，勿停衣糧。

translations.literal: Those disabled and ruined from wounds in battle—do not cease clothing and grain.
translations.idiomatic: those permanently disabled by wounds continued to receive their rations without interruption.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丙戌朔，上御興安門受俘，遂以吳元濟獻廟社，斬於獨柳之下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, first day of cycle bingxu, the emperor presided at Xing'an Gate to receive captives, then offered Wu Yuanji to the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain, and executed him beneath the Lone Willow.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eleventh month, bingxu, the emperor received prisoners at Xing'an Gate, offered Wu Yuanji to the ancestral temples, and executed him beneath the Lone Willow.
