sentences.zh: 初，淮西之人劫於李希烈、吳少誠之威虐，不能自拔，久而老者衰，幼者壯，安於悖逆，不復知有朝廷矣。

translations.literal: Initially the people of Huaixi were coerced by the brutal tyranny of Li Xilie and Wu Shaocheng and could not extricate themselves; over time the old weakened, the young grew strong, settled into rebellion, and again knew not that there was a court.
translations.idiomatic: At first the people of Huaixi were trapped under the tyranny of Li Xilie and Wu Shaocheng. Generations passed: the old died, the young grew up knowing only rebellion, with no memory of the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 自少誠以來，遣諸將出兵，皆不束以法制，聽各以便宜自戰，故人人得盡其才。

translations.literal: From Shaocheng onward, when sending generals out with troops, none were bound by law and regulation—each was allowed to fight as expedient dictated—therefore every man could exhaust his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Since Wu Shaocheng's day, generals sent into the field were not bound by rigid rules. Each was left to fight as he saw fit, and so every commander could use his talents fully.

sentences.zh: 韓全義之敗於殷水也，於其帳中得朝貴所與問訊書，少誠束而示眾曰：「此皆公卿屬全義書，雲破蔡州日，乞一將士妻女為婢妾。」

translations.literal: When Han Quanyi was defeated at Yinshui, in his tent they obtained letters from court nobles to him inquiring after him; Shaocheng bound them and showed the host, saying, "These are all letters from chief ministers to Quanyi, saying on the day Cai Prefecture is broken, they beg one officer's wife or daughter as servant-concubine.
translations.idiomatic: After Han Quanyi's defeat at Yinshui, letters from court officials were found in his tent. Wu Shaocheng had them bound up and read aloud: "These ministers wrote to Quanyi promising that when Caizhou fell, each wanted a soldier's wife or daughter for his concubine.

sentences.zh: 由是眾皆憤怒，以死為賊用。

translations.literal: From this the host all grew furious and served the rebels unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were furious and fought for the rebels as if their lives depended on it.

sentences.zh: 雖居中士，其風俗獷戾，過於夷貊。

translations.literal: Though in the central realm, their customs were fierce and cruel, surpassing the barbarians of Yi and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Though they lived in the heart of China, their ways were more brutal than those of the frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 故以三州之眾，舉天下之兵環而攻之，四年然後克之。

translations.literal: Therefore with the population of three prefectures, the armies of all under heaven encircled and attacked them—four years before they were overcome.
translations.idiomatic: With only three prefectures' worth of men they held off the armies of the entire empire for four years before they fell.

sentences.zh: 官軍之攻元濟也，李師道募人通使於蔡，察其形勢，牙前虞候劉晏平應募，出汴、宋間，潛行至蔡。

translations.literal: When the government army attacked Yuanji, Li Shidao recruited men to serve as envoys to Cai to observe the situation; Forward Guard Officer Liu Yanping answered the call, went out between Bian and Song, and secretly traveled to Cai.
translations.idiomatic: While the imperial army besieged Wu Yuanji, Li Shidao hired scouts to report on conditions in Caizhou. Forward Guard Officer Liu Yanping volunteered, crossed through Bian and Song, and slipped into the city.

sentences.zh: 元濟大喜，厚禮而遣之。

translations.literal: Yuanji was greatly pleased, treated him generously, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yuanji was delighted, treated him lavishly, and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 晏平還至鄆，師道屏人而問之，晏平曰：「元濟暴兵數萬於外，阽危如此，而日與僕妾遊戲博奕於內，晏然曾無憂色。

translations.literal: Yanping returned to Yun; Shidao dismissed others and questioned him. Yanping said, "Yuanji has tens of thousands of troops deployed outside in peril such as this, yet daily with servants and concubines plays games and gambles within—serene, never a look of worry.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yanping returned to Yunzhou, Li Shidao questioned him in private. Yanping said, "Wu Yuanji has tens of thousands of men in the field and the situation is desperate, yet he spends his days gambling with servants and concubines. He shows no worry at all.

sentences.zh: 以愚觀之，殆必亡，不久矣！」

translations.literal: In this fool's view, he will surely perish—not long from now!
translations.idiomatic: In my view he is doomed, and soon!

sentences.zh: 師道素倚淮西為援，聞之驚怒，尋誣以他過，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Shidao had long relied on Huaixi as support; hearing this he was alarmed and enraged, and soon framed him on another fault and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao had counted on Huaixi as his ally. Shocked and furious at the report, he soon found a pretext and had Liu Yanping beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以李愬為山南東道節度使，賜爵涼國公；

translations.literal: On day wuzi Li Su was made Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit and ennobled Duke of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Li Su was appointed Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit and created Duke of Liang;

sentences.zh: 加韓弘兼侍中；

translations.literal: Han Hong was additionally made Palace Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong was promoted to Palace Attendant;

sentences.zh: 李光顏、烏重胤等各遷官有差。

translations.literal: Li Guangyan, Wu Chongyin, and others each were transferred in office with varying grades.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangyan, Wu Chongyin, and others received various promotions.

sentences.zh: 舊制，御史二人知驛。

translations.literal: By old regulation two censors supervised the relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: By custom two censors oversaw the post stations.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，詔以宦者為館驛使。

translations.literal: On day renchen an edict appointed eunuchs as Postal Station Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen the throne ordered eunuchs appointed as postal commissioners.

sentences.zh: 左補闕裴潾諫曰：「內臣外事，職分各殊，切在塞侵官之源，絕出位之漸。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Official Pei Lin remonstrated, saying, "Inner servants and outer affairs—their duties are each distinct; it is urgent to block the source of encroachment on offices and cut off the gradual overstepping of rank.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Official Pei Lin warned, "Palace eunuchs and state business belong to separate spheres. We must stop the first step toward encroachment on civil authority.

sentences.zh: 事有不便，必戒於初；

translations.literal: When matters are inconvenient, one must take warning at the beginning;
translations.idiomatic: When a policy is wrong, catch it at the start;

sentences.zh: 令或有妨，不必在大。」

translations.literal: When orders may have impediments, it need not be in something large.
translations.idiomatic: Even a small abuse can lead to grave harm.

sentences.zh: 上不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 甲午，恩王連薨。

translations.literal: On day jiawu Prince En Lian passed away.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Prince En, Lian, died.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以唐、隨兵馬使李祐為神武將軍，知軍事。

translations.literal: On day xinchou Tang and Sui Army Horse Commissioner Li You was made General of Spirit Martial and given charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Li You, army horse commissioner for Tang and Sui, was appointed General of Divine Martiality and put in command.

sentences.zh: 裴度以馬總為彰義留兵。

translations.literal: Pei Du left Ma Zong as garrison troops of Zhangyi.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du left Ma Zong as acting commander of the Zhangyi garrison.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，發蔡州。

translations.literal: On day guichou he departed from Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Pei Du departed from Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 上封二劍以授梁守謙，使誅吳元濟舊將。

translations.literal: The emperor sealed two swords and entrusted them to Liang Shouqian, ordering the execution of Wu Yuanji's old generals.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sealed two swords and gave them to Liang Shouqian with orders to execute Wu Yuanji's former generals.

sentences.zh: 度至郾城，遇之，復與俱入蔡州，量罪施刑，不盡如詔旨，仍上疏言之。

translations.literal: Du reached Yancheng, encountered him, and again entered Cai with him; measuring crimes and applying punishments, not wholly as the edict directed—still he submitted a memorial stating this.
translations.idiomatic: At Yancheng Pei Du met Liang Shouqian and returned with him to Caizhou. He meted out punishments by degree of guilt and did not carry out the full slaughter the edict demanded, then memorialized the emperor to explain.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬戌，賜裴度爵晉國公，復入知政事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, day renxu, Pei Du was ennobled Duke of Jin and again entered to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renxu, Pei Du was created Duke of Jin and returned to the chief councilorship.

sentences.zh: 以馬總為淮西節度使。

translations.literal: Ma Zong was made Military Governor of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong was appointed Military Governor of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 初，吐突承璀方貴寵用事，為淮南監軍。

translations.literal: Initially Tu Gu Chenghuan was then in noble favor wielding power, serving as Army Supervisor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the eunuch Tu Gu Chenghuan was in favor and wielded power as army supervisor in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 李鄘為節度使，性剛嚴，與承璀互相敬憚，故未嘗相失。

translations.literal: Li Yong was Military Governor; his nature was stern and severe; he and Chenghuan mutually respected and feared each other, and therefore never lost accord.
translations.idiomatic: Military Governor Li Yong was stern by nature. He and Chenghuan respected and feared each other in equal measure, and so never clashed.

sentences.zh: 承璀歸，引鄘為相。

translations.literal: Chenghuan returned and brought Yong forward as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenghuan returned to court he recommended Li Yong for chancellor.

sentences.zh: 鄘恥由宦官進，及將佐出祖，樂作，鄘泣下曰：「吾老安外鎮，宰相非吾任也！」

translations.literal: Yong was shamed at advancing through eunuchs; when his officers and aides came to send him off and music played, Yong wept and said, "I am old and secure in an outer command—the chancellorship is not my charge!
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong was ashamed to owe his promotion to a eunuch. When his staff came to see him off with music, he wept and said, "I am an old man fit to die in a border post. The chancellorship is not my place!

sentences.zh: 戊寅，鄘至京師，辭疾，不入見，不視事，百官到門，皆辭不見。

translations.literal: On day wuyin Yong reached the capital, pleaded illness, did not enter audience, did not attend to duties; officials of all ranks came to his gate—all were declined, none received.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Li Yong reached the capital, pleaded illness, refused audience, and declined to take office. Officials who came to his gate were all turned away.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，貶淮西降將董重質為春州司戶。

translations.literal: On day gengchen the surrendered Huai West general Dong Chongzhi was demoted to Registrar of Chun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen the former Huai Xi general Dong Chongzhi was demoted to registrar of Chun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 重質為吳元濟謀主，屢破官軍。

translations.literal: Chongzhi was Wu Yuanji's chief strategist and repeatedly routed the government army.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chongzhi had been Wu Yuanji's chief strategist and had beaten the imperial army many times.

sentences.zh: 上欲殺之，李愬奏先許重質以不死。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to kill him; Li Su memorialized that he had first promised Chongzhi he would not die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted him executed, but Li Su reminded him that he had promised Dong Chongzhi his life.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝中之下元和十三年（

translations.literal: Mid-lower of Emperor Xianzong Zhaowen Zhangwu Dasheng Zhishen Xiaohuangdi, Yuanyuan thirteenth year (
translations.idiomatic: Mid-lower segment of the reign of Emperor Xianzong, Yuanyuan year 13 (

sentences.zh: 戊戌，公元八一八年）

translations.literal: day wuxu, the year CE eight one eight)
translations.idiomatic: wuxu, CE 818)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙酉朔，赦天下。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, first day of cycle yiyou, amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, yiyou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 初，李師道謀逆命，判官高沐與同僚郭日戶、李公度屢諫之。

translations.literal: Initially Li Shidao plotted rebellion; Judge Gao Mu with colleagues Guo Rihu and Li Gongdu repeatedly remonstrated with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Shidao began plotting rebellion, his secretary Gao Mu, along with colleagues Guo Rihu and Li Gongdu, repeatedly warned him against it.

sentences.zh: 判官李文會、孔目官林英素為師道所親信，涕泣言於師道曰：「文會等盡誠為尚書憂家事，反為高沐等所疾，尚書奈何不憂十二州之土地，以成沐等之功名乎！」

translations.literal: Judge Li Wenhuì and chief clerk Lin Ying were always trusted by Shidao; weeping they said to Shidao, "Wenhuì and others exhaust sincerity in worrying over the Governor's family affairs, yet are hated by Gao Mu and the rest—Governor, why not worry over the land of twelve prefectures and complete Mu and the rest with meritorious fame!
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Li Wenhuì and chief clerk Lin Ying, favorites of Li Shidao, wept before him and said, "We serve you faithfully, yet Gao Mu and his friends hate us. Will you sacrifice the twelve prefectures just to make them famous?

sentences.zh: 師道由是疏沐等，出沐知萊州。

translations.literal: Shidao from this kept Mu and the rest at a distance and sent Mu out as prefect of Lai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao then distanced himself from Gao Mu and sent him out as prefect of Lai.

sentences.zh: 會林英入奏事，令進奏吏密申師道云：「沐潛輸款於朝廷。」

translations.literal: When Lin Ying went in to report affairs to the throne, he had the memorial courier secretly inform Shidao, saying, "Mu secretly sends pledges of loyalty to the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin Ying went to court he had the memorial courier secretly tell Li Shidao, "Gao Mu is secretly negotiating with the throne.

sentences.zh: 文會從而構之，師道殺沐，並囚郭日戶，凡軍中勸師道效順者，文會皆指為高沐之黨而囚之。

translations.literal: Wenhuì followed with framing him; Shidao killed Mu and also imprisoned Guo Rihu; all in the army who urged Shidao to submit to obedience—Wenhuì pointed to all as Gao Mu's faction and imprisoned them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wenhuì built on the accusation. Li Shidao executed Gao Mu and imprisoned Guo Rihu. Everyone in the army who urged submission was denounced as Gao Mu's ally and thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 及淮西平，師道憂懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, Shidao was anxious and afraid, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: When Huai Xi fell, Li Shidao was terrified and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 李公度及牙將李英曇因其懼而說之，使納質獻地以自贖。

translations.literal: Li Gongdu and guard general Li Yingtan, taking advantage of his fear, persuaded him to send hostages and cede territory to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongdu and guard general Li Yingtan seized on his fear and persuaded him to send a hostage, surrender territory, and buy his way back into favor.

sentences.zh: 師道從之，遣使奉表，請使長子入侍，並獻沂、密、海三州。

translations.literal: Shidao followed this, sent envoys with a memorial, requesting to send his eldest son to serve at court, and also offered the three prefectures Yi, Mi, and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao agreed, sent envoys with a petition offering his eldest son as hostage at court and ceding Yi, Mi, and Hai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遣左常侍李遜詣鄆州宣慰。

translations.literal: On day yisi the Left Regular Attendant Li Xun was dispatched to Yun Prefecture to proclaim reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Left Regular Attendant Li Xun was sent to Yunzhou with words of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 上命六軍修麟德殿。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the Six Armies to repair the Linde Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the Six Armies to renovate Linde Hall.

sentences.zh: 右龍武統軍張奉國、大將軍李文悅以外寇初平，營繕太多，白宰相，冀有論諫。

translations.literal: Right Dragon Martial Commander-in-Chief Zhang Fengguo and Grand General Li Wenyue, because external enemies had just been pacified and camp repairs were excessive, reported to the chancellor, hoping there would be discussion and remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fengguo, commander of the Right Dragon Martial Army, and Grand General Li Wenyue, noting that the frontier had only just been quieted while military camps were being overhauled at great expense, informed the chancellor in the hope that someone at court would speak up.

sentences.zh: 裴度因奏事言之。

translations.literal: Pei Du, while presenting business at audience, spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du raised the matter when he came before the emperor on other business.

sentences.zh: 上怒，二月，丁卯，以奉國為鴻臚卿，壬申，以文悅為右武衛大將軍，充威遠營使。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry. In the second month, on dingmao Fengguo was made Director of the Court of Banquets; on renshen Wenyue was made General of the Right Martial Guard and made Commissioner of the Weiyuan Camp.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. In the second month, on dingmao he demoted Zhang Fengguo to director of the Court of Banquets; on renshen he made Li Wenyue general of the Right Martial Guard and commissioner of the Weiyuan camp.

sentences.zh: 於是浚龍首池，起承暉殿，土木浸興矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon they dredged Longshou Pool and raised Chenghui Hall—earthworks and timber work gradually flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Construction then surged: Longshou Pool was dredged, Chenghui Hall was raised, and palace building projects multiplied.

sentences.zh: 李愬奏請判官、大將以下官凡百五十員，上不悅，謂裴度曰：「李愬誠有奇功，然奏請過多。

translations.literal: Li Su memorialized requesting one hundred fifty posts from adjutant and chief general downward. The emperor was displeased and said to Pei Du: "Li Su truly has marvelous merit, yet his requests are excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su petitioned for one hundred fifty appointments, from adjutants down through chief generals. The emperor was displeased and told Pei Du, "Li Su has indeed done extraordinary service, but this request goes too far.

sentences.zh: 使如李晟、渾瑊，又何如哉！」

translations.literal: If it were like Li Sheng or Hun Jian, how would that be!
translations.idiomatic: Would men like Li Sheng or Hun Jian ever ask for so much?

sentences.zh: 遂留中不下。

translations.literal: The memorial was therefore held at court and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The petition was shelved and never approved.

sentences.zh: 李鄘固辭相位，戊戌，以鄘為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Li Yong firmly declined the chancellorship. On wuxu Yong was made Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yong steadfastly refused the chancellorship. On wuxu he was appointed minister of revenue instead.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫李夷簡為門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Yijian was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Li Yijian was made vice director of the Secretariat and associate chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，渤海僖王言義卒，弟簡王明忠立，改元太始；

translations.literal: Previously, the Parhae Prince Xiyi Yanyi died; his younger brother Jian Wang Mingzhong succeeded and changed the era name to Taishi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Xiyi Yanyi of Parhae had died. His younger brother Jian Wang Mingzhong succeeded him and proclaimed the era Taishi.

sentences.zh: 一歲卒，從父仁秀立，改元建興。

translations.literal: After one year he died; his paternal uncle Renxiu succeeded and changed the era name to Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Mingzhong died in turn, and his uncle Renxiu took the throne, changing the era name to Jianxing.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遣使來告喪。

translations.literal: On yisi envoys were sent to report the mourning.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Parhae sent envoys to announce the new death.

sentences.zh: 橫海節度使程權自以世襲滄景，與河朔三鎮無殊，內不自安。

translations.literal: Heng Hai Military Governor Cheng Quan considered that his hereditary hold on Cang and Jing was no different from the three Hebei circuits, and was inwardly uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Quan, military governor of Heng Hai, knew that his family's hereditary hold on Cangzhou and Jingzhou made him no different from the three Hebei warlords, and he could not rest easy.

sentences.zh: 己酉，遣使上表，請舉族入朝，許之。

translations.literal: On jiyou he sent envoys with a memorial requesting that his entire clan enter court; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he sent a memorial asking to bring his whole clan to court, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 橫海將士樂自擅，不聽權去，掌書記林蘊諭以禍福，權乃得出。

translations.literal: Heng Hai officers and soldiers were pleased to hold power themselves and would not let Quan leave. Chief Secretary Lin Yun explained fortune and calamity, and only then was Quan able to depart.
translations.idiomatic: The Heng Hai troops enjoyed their autonomy and refused to let Cheng Quan go. Chief secretary Lin Yun reasoned with them about the consequences, and only then was Quan able to leave.

sentences.zh: 詔以蘊為禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Yun Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Lin Yun vice director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 裴度之在淮西也，布衣柏耆以策干韓愈曰：「吳元濟既就擒，王承宗破膽矣，願得奉丞相書往說之，可不煩兵而服。」

translations.literal: When Pei Du was in Huai Xi, the commoner Bai Qi presented a plan to Han Yu, saying: "Now that Wu Yuanji has been captured, Wang Chengzong's courage is broken. I wish to carry the Chancellor's letter to go persuade him—it can be done without troubling troops and he will submit.
translations.idiomatic: While Pei Du was in Huai Xi, a commoner named Bai Qi sought out Han Yu with a proposal: "Wu Yuanji is already taken, and Wang Chengzong's nerve is broken. Give me the chancellor's letter to carry to him, and he may submit without another campaign.

sentences.zh: 愈白度，為書遣之。

translations.literal: Yu reported to Du, who wrote a letter and dispatched him.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu told Pei Du, who wrote the letter and sent Bai Qi on his way.

sentences.zh: 承宗懼，求哀於田弘正，請以二子為質，及獻德、棣二州，輸租稅，請官史。

translations.literal: Chengzong was afraid, begged Tian Hongzheng for mercy, requested to send two sons as hostages, and to cede De and Di Prefectures, pay taxes, and request official clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wang Chengzong appealed to Tian Hongzheng, offering his two sons as hostages, surrendering De and Di prefectures, paying taxes, and accepting imperial officials.

sentences.zh: 弘正為之奏請，上初不許；

translations.literal: Hongzheng memorialized on his behalf; at first the emperor did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng memorialized on his behalf, but at first the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 弘正上表相繼，上重違弘正意，乃許之。

translations.literal: Hongzheng sent memorials in succession; the emperor, loath to violate Hongzheng's intent, then granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng sent one memorial after another, and the emperor, unwilling to reject him outright, finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅朔，魏博遣使送承宗子知感、知信及德、棣二州圖印至京師。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, first day jiayin—the Weibo circuit sent envoys delivering Chengzong's sons Zhigan and Zhixin plus the maps and seals of De and Di Prefectures to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, jiayin, Weibo sent envoys to the capital with Chengzong's sons Zhigan and Zhixin and the maps and seals of De and Di prefectures.

sentences.zh: 幽州大將譚忠說劉總曰：「自元和以來，劉辟、李錡、田季安、盧從史、吳元濟，阻兵憑險，自以為深根固蒂，天下莫能危也。

translations.literal: Youzhou major general Tan Zhong advised Liu Zong, saying: "Since the Yuanhe era, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Tian Ji'an, Lu Congshi, and Wu Yuanji have held armies and relied on perilous terrain, thinking themselves deeply rooted and firm—none in the realm could harm them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Zhong, a senior general in Youzhou, urged Liu Zong: "Since the Yuanhe reign, Liu Pi, Li Qi, Tian Ji'an, Lu Congshi, and Wu Yuanji all held armies behind strong defenses and believed their power was too deep-rooted for anyone to touch.

sentences.zh: 然顧盼之間，身死家覆，皆不自知，此非人力所能及，殆天誅也。

translations.literal: Yet in the turning of an eye they died and their clans were destroyed, not knowing it themselves—this is not something human power can reach; it is nearly heaven's punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in a blink they were dead and their houses ruined, never seeing it coming. That was beyond human contrivance—it was heaven's judgment.

sentences.zh: 況今天子神聖威武，苦身焦思，縮衣節食，以養戰士，此志豈須臾忘天下哉！

translations.literal: Moreover today's Son of Heaven is sacred, divine, and martially awesome—he toils his body and burns his thoughts, cuts clothing and limits food to nourish the warriors. Would he for a moment forget the realm!
translations.idiomatic: And today's emperor is resolute and formidable: he wears himself down, eats sparingly, and feeds his soldiers for war. Do you think he will forget the realm for an instant?

sentences.zh: 今國兵駸駸北來，趙人已獻城十二，忠深為公憂之。」

translations.literal: Now the imperial army presses northward; the Zhao people have already surrendered twelve cities—Zhong is deeply worried for you.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies are already pressing north, and twelve Zhao cities have surrendered. I am deeply worried for you, my lord.

sentences.zh: 總泣且拜曰：「聞先生言，吾心定矣。」

translations.literal: Zong wept and bowed, saying: "Having heard the Master's words, my mind is settled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zong wept and bowed. "Hearing you, sir, my mind is made up.

sentences.zh: 遂專意歸朝廷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he devoted himself wholly to returning to the court.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he set his whole purpose on returning to imperial allegiance.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，內出廢印二紐，賜左、右三軍辟仗使。

translations.literal: On wuchen the inner palace issued two discarded seals and bestowed them on the left and right Three Armies ritual guard commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen the palace issued two retired official seals and granted them to the left and right Three Armies ritual guard commissioners.

sentences.zh: 舊制，以宦官為六軍辟仗使，如方鎮之監軍，無印。

translations.literal: Under the old system, eunuchs served as Six Armies ritual guard commissioners, like circuit army supervisors—without seals.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom eunuchs held the Six Armies ritual guard posts, much like circuit army supervisors, but without official seals.

sentences.zh: 及張奉國等得罪，至是始賜印，得糾繩軍政，事任專達矣。

translations.literal: After Zhang Fengguo and others offended, only then were seals granted, enabling them to inspect and regulate military affairs—their responsibilities became exclusively reported.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Fengguo and the others fell from favor, seals were granted for the first time, giving these eunuchs authority to discipline army affairs and report directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，詔洗雪王承宗及成德將士，復其官爵。

translations.literal: On gengchen an edict cleared Wang Chengzong and the Chengde officers and soldiers, restoring their ranks and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen an edict cleared Wang Chengzong and the Chengde garrison of blame and restored their ranks and titles.

sentences.zh: 李師道闇弱，軍府大事，獨與妻魏氏、奴胡惟堪、楊自溫、婢蒲氏、袁氏及孔目官王再升謀之，大將及幕僚莫得預焉。

translations.literal: Li Shidao was dim and weak; on major military commission affairs he consulted only with his wife Lady Wei, the slaves Hu Weikan and Yang Ziwen, the maidservants Lady Pu and Lady Yuan, and the clerk Wang Zaishang—the generals and staff could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao was dull and indecisive. Great affairs of the command were decided only with his wife Lady Wei, the slaves Hu Weikan and Yang Ziwen, the maidservants Pu and Yuan, and the clerk Wang Zaishang; his generals and staff were shut out.

sentences.zh: 魏氏不欲其子入質，與蒲氏、袁氏言於師道曰：「自先司徒以來，有此十二州，奈何無故割而獻之！

translations.literal: Lady Wei did not want her son sent as hostage; together with Ladies Pu and Yuan she said to Shidao: "Since the late Minister of Works, we have held these twelve prefectures—how can we for no reason cede and offer them!
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei did not want her son sent as a hostage. With Pu and Yuan she told Shidao, "Since your father's day we have held these twelve prefectures—why surrender them for nothing?

sentences.zh: 今計境內之兵不下數十萬，不獻三州，不過以兵相加。

translations.literal: Now counting the troops within our borders, they are no fewer than several hundred thousand; if we do not cede three prefectures, it is no more than meeting force with force.
translations.idiomatic: We still have several hundred thousand troops in the circuit. If we refuse to give up three prefectures, at worst we fight.

sentences.zh: 若力戰不勝，獻之未晚。」

translations.literal: If we fight with all our strength and do not win, ceding them will not be too late.
translations.idiomatic: If we fight with everything we have and still lose, it will not be too late to surrender then.

sentences.zh: 師道乃大悔，欲殺李公度，幕僚賈直言謂其用事奴曰：「今大禍將至，豈非高沐冤氣所為！

translations.literal: Shidao then deeply regretted it and wished to kill Li Gongdu. Staff member Jia Zhiyan said to the powerful slaves: "Now great calamity is about to arrive—is this not the work of Gao Mu's wronged spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Shidao deeply regretted his earlier concessions and wanted Li Gongdu killed. Staff officer Jia Zhiyan told the slaves who ran the command, "Disaster is coming—is this not the vengeful spirit of Gao Mu?

sentences.zh: 若又殺公度，軍府其危哉！」

translations.literal: If you kill Gongdu again, the military commission will be in peril!
translations.idiomatic: If you kill Gongdu too, the whole command will be finished!

sentences.zh: 乃囚之。

translations.literal: He was therefore imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gongdu was imprisoned instead.

sentences.zh: 遷李英曇於萊州，未至，縊殺之。

translations.literal: Li Yingtan was transferred to Laizhou; before he arrived he was strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yingtan was reassigned to Laizhou, but before he arrived he was strangled.

sentences.zh: 李遜至鄆州，師逆大陣兵迎之，遜盛氣正色，為陳禍福，責其決語，欲白天子。

translations.literal: Li Xun reached Yan Prefecture; Shidao deployed his great battle array to welcome him. Xun was imposing in bearing and stern in countenance, explained fortune and calamity, demanded a decisive reply, and intended to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun reached Yanzhou, Shidao met him with a massive display of force. Xun held his ground, laid out the stakes, demanded a clear answer, and threatened to report everything to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 師道退，與其黨謀之，皆曰：「弟許之，他日正煩一表解紛耳。」

translations.literal: Shidao withdrew and consulted his faction; all said: "Your younger brother can agree to it—another day it will only take one memorial to clear up the trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao withdrew to consult his followers, who said, "Agree for now, my lord—later a single memorial will settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 師道乃謝曰：「向以父子之私，且迫於將士之情，故遷延未遣。

translations.literal: Shidao then apologized, saying: "Previously, because of private feelings between father and son and also pressed by the soldiers' sentiments, I delayed and did not send them.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao then apologized: "I delayed because of family feeling and pressure from the troops.

sentences.zh: 今重煩朝使，豈敢復有二三！」

translations.literal: Now having again troubled the court envoy, how dare I again have any second thoughts!
translations.idiomatic: Now that the court has sent you again, how could I hesitate any longer?

sentences.zh: 遜察師道非實誠，歸，言於上曰：「師道頑愚反覆，恐必須用兵。」

translations.literal: Xun perceived that Shidao was not sincere; upon return he said to the emperor: "Shidao is stubborn, foolish, and changeable—I fear troops will necessarily have to be used.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun saw that Shidao was insincere. Back at court he told the emperor, "Shidao is obstinate, foolish, and unreliable. I fear force will be necessary.

sentences.zh: 既而師道表言軍情，不聽納質割地，上怒，決意討之。

translations.literal: Then Shidao memorialized stating army sentiment—he would not accept sending hostages or ceding territory. The emperor was angry and resolved to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Shidao memorialized that his army would not accept hostages or territorial concessions. The emperor was enraged and resolved on campaign.

sentences.zh: 賈直言冒刃諫師道者二：輿櫬諫者一，又畫縛載檻車妻子係累者以獻。

translations.literal: Jia Zhiyan twice remonstrated Shidao while risking the blade; one man remonstrated carrying a coffin; he also painted bound figures of wife and children loaded on a caged cart in chains and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Zhiyan twice remonstrated at sword's point; one adviser came with a coffin on his back; Jia also presented a painting of a bound family loaded into a prison cart.

sentences.zh: 師道怒，囚之。

translations.literal: Shidao was angry and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao had him imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙申，以忠武節度使李光顏為義成節度使，謀討師道也。

translations.literal: Fifth month, bingchen—the Zhongwu Military Governor Li Guangyan was made Yicheng Military Governor, planning to attack Shidao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, Li Guangyan was moved from Zhongwu to Yicheng in preparation for the campaign against Shidao.

sentences.zh: 以淮西節度使馬總為忠武節度使，陳、許、殷、蔡州觀察使。

translations.literal: Huai Xi Military Governor Ma Cong was made Zhongwu Military Governor and Military Commissioner of Chen, Xu, Yin, and Cai Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zong, military governor of Huai Xi, was made military governor of Zhongwu and commissioner over Chen, Xu, Yin, and Cai.

sentences.zh: 以申州隸鄂岳，光州隸淮南。

translations.literal: Shen Prefecture was placed under E-Yue; Guang Prefecture under Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhou was placed under E-Yue, and Guangzhou under Huainan.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以知勃海國務大仁秀為勃海王。

translations.literal: On xinchou Renxiu, who managed Parhae state affairs, was made King of Parhae.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Renxiu, who had been managing Parhae affairs, was enthroned as king of Parhae.

sentences.zh: 以河陽都知兵馬使曹華為棣州刺史，詔以河陽兵二千送至商河。

translations.literal: He-Yang Command of Troops Cavalry Officer Cao Hua was made Prefect of Di Prefecture; an edict ordered two thousand He-Yang troops escorted to Shanghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Hua, He-Yang commander of troops and cavalry, was appointed prefect of Di Prefecture, with two thousand He-Yang soldiers ordered to escort him to Shanghe.

sentences.zh: 會縣為平盧兵所陷，華擊卻之，殺二千餘人，復其縣以聞。

translations.literal: When the county was captured by Pinglu troops, Hua struck and repelled them, killed more than two thousand, recovered the county, and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When the county fell to Pinglu troops, Hua counterattacked, killed more than two thousand of the enemy, recovered the county, and reported his success.

sentences.zh: 詔加橫海節度副使。

translations.literal: An edict added him as Vice Military Governor of Heng Hai.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted him to vice military governor of Heng Hai.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day guichou—the sun was eclipsed.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the sixth month, guichou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，復以烏重胤領懷州刺史，鎮河陽。

translations.literal: On dingchou Wu Chongyin was again made Prefect of Huai Prefecture and stationed at He-Yang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wu Chongyin was again made prefect of Huai Prefecture and posted at He-Yang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸未朔，徙李愬為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day guimwei—Li Su was transferred to Military Governor of Wu-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, guimwei, Li Su was transferred to military governor of Wu-Ning.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，下制罪狀李師道，令宣武、魏博、義成、武寧、橫海兵共討之，以宣歙觀察使王遂為供軍使。

translations.literal: On yiyou an imperial rescript listed Li Shidao's crimes and ordered armies of Xuan-Wu, Weibo, Yicheng, Wu-Ning, and Heng Hai jointly to attack him; Xuan-She Military Commissioner Wang Sui was made Army Supply Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou an imperial decree condemned Li Shidao and ordered the armies of Xuan-Wu, Weibo, Yicheng, Wu-Ning, and Heng Hai to attack him jointly, with Wang Sui, commissioner of Xuan-She, appointed army supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 遂，方慶之孫也。

translations.literal: Sui was Fang Qing's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sui was a grandson of Fang Qing.

sentences.zh: 上方委裴度以用兵，門下侍郎、同平章事李夷簡自謂才不及度，求出鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor was then entrusting military affairs to Pei Du; Vice Director and Associate Chancellor Li Yijian considered his talent inferior to Du's and requested to go out to a command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was entrusting the war to Pei Du. Li Yijian, vice director and associate chancellor, felt himself outmatched and asked for a provincial command.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以夷簡同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: On xinchou Yijian was made Associate Chancellor and Huainan Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Li Yijian was kept as associate chancellor and sent out as military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬子朔，中書侍郎、同平章事王涯罷為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Eighth month, first day renzi—Central Vice Director and Associate Chancellor Wang Ya was removed and made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the eighth month, renzi, Wang Ya was removed from the chancellorship and made vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 吳元濟既平，韓弘懼；

translations.literal: After Wu Yuanji was pacified, Han Hong was afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wu Yuanji was crushed, Han Hong grew fearful.

sentences.zh: 九月，自將兵擊李師道，圍曹州。

translations.literal: Ninth month—he personally led troops to attack Li Shidao and besieged Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he personally led troops against Li Shidao and besieged Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 淮西既平，上浸驕侈。

translations.literal: After Huai Xi was pacified, the emperor gradually grew proud and extravagant.
translations.idiomatic: With Huai Xi pacified, the emperor grew increasingly proud and extravagant.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎判度支皇甫鎛、衛尉卿、鹽鐵轉運使程異曉其意，數進羨餘以供其費，由是有寵。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue supervising the Treasury Huangfu Bo and Director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner Cheng Yi understood his intent; they repeatedly presented surpluses to supply his expenses—thereby gaining favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, vice minister of revenue in charge of the treasury, and Cheng Yi, director of the Court of Imperial Regalia and salt and iron transport commissioner, read the emperor's mood and repeatedly offered surplus revenue for his pleasures, and so won favor.

sentences.zh: 鎛又厚賂結吐突承璀。

translations.literal: Bo also heavily bribed and bonded with Tu Gu Chenghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo also lavished bribes on the eunuch Tu Gu Chenghuan.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，鎛以本官、異以工部侍郎並同平章事，判使如故。

translations.literal: On jiachen Bo with his existing office and Yi as Vice Minister of Works were both made Associate Chancellors; their supervision posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Huangfu Bo kept his existing offices and Cheng Yi was made vice minister of works; both were appointed associate chancellors while retaining their fiscal posts.

sentences.zh: 制下，朝野駭愕，至於市井負販者亦嗤之。

translations.literal: When the rescript was issued, court and countryside were shocked; even market peddlers scoffed.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, court and country were appalled—even street peddlers laughed.

sentences.zh: 裴度、崔群極陳其不可，上不聽。

translations.literal: Pei Du and Cui Qun urgently argued it was impossible—the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du and Cui Qun protested vigorously, but the emperor would not hear them.

sentences.zh: 度恥與小人同列，表求自退。

translations.literal: Du was ashamed to stand in rank with petty men and memorialized requesting to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed to serve alongside such men, Pei Du asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was refused.

sentences.zh: 度復上疏，以為：「鎛、異皆錢穀吏，佞巧小人，陛下一旦置之相位，中外無不駭笑。

translations.literal: Du again submitted a memorial, stating: "Bo and Yi are both grain and money clerks—sycophantic, artful petty men. Your Majesty suddenly placed them in chancellor rank—inside and outside there is none who is not shocked and laughing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du submitted another memorial: "Huangfu Bo and Cheng Yi are mere finance clerks—sycophantic men of low character. To elevate them to the chancellorship at once has shocked and amused everyone inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 況鎛在度支，專以豐取刻與為務，凡中外仰給度支之人無不思食其肉。

translations.literal: Moreover Bo in the Treasury devoted himself solely to extorting and scraping; all within and without who depended on the Treasury for support none did not wish to eat his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Worse, as head of the treasury Huangfu Bo made squeezing and scraping his whole business; everyone who depended on treasury funds would gladly see him dead.

sentences.zh: 比者裁損淮西糧料，軍士怨怒。

translations.literal: Recently he cut Huai Xi grain rations; the soldiers were resentful and angry.
translations.idiomatic: He has lately cut Huai Xi rations, and the soldiers are furious.

sentences.zh: 會臣至行營曉諭慰勉，僅無潰亂。

translations.literal: When Your subject reached the field camp to explain, comfort, and encourage, barely there was no mutiny and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Only when I went to the camps myself to explain and reassure them was a mutiny barely averted.

sentences.zh: 今舊將舊兵悉向淄青，聞鎛入相，必盡驚憂，知無可訴之地矣。

translations.literal: Now the old generals and old soldiers all turn toward Ziqing; hearing Bo enter the chancellorship, they will certainly all be shocked and worried, knowing there is no place left to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Now the veteran generals and troops are marching on Ziqing. When they hear that Huangfu Bo has become chancellor, they will be terrified, knowing they have nowhere left to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 程異雖人品庸下，然心事和平，可處煩劇，不宜為相。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi although his personal character is mediocre and low, yet his mind and affairs are peaceful; he can handle heavy and urgent work—he is not fit to be chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi is a lesser man, but steady in temperament and capable with heavy administrative work—still, he should not be chancellor.

sentences.zh: 至如鎛，資性狡詐，天下共知，唯能上惑聖聰，足見奸邪之極。

translations.literal: As for Bo, his native disposition is cunning and deceitful—the realm jointly knows it; he can only beguile the sacred clarity above, sufficient to show the extreme of treachery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bo, by contrast, is cunning and deceitful—everyone knows it. That he can delude Your Majesty alone shows how utterly corrupt he is.

sentences.zh: 臣若不退，天下謂臣不知廉恥；

translations.literal: If Your subject does not withdraw, the realm will say Your subject does not know shame and honor.
translations.idiomatic: If I do not resign, the world will say I have no sense of shame;

sentences.zh: 臣若不言，天下謂臣有負恩寵。

translations.literal: If Your subject does not speak, the realm will say Your subject has failed favored grace.
translations.idiomatic: if I do not speak out, the world will say I have betrayed your favor.

sentences.zh: 今退既不許，言又不聽，臣如烈火燒心，眾鏑叢體。

translations.literal: Now withdrawal is not permitted and speaking is not heeded—I am like fire burning the heart, many arrows piercing the body.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am forbidden to resign and ignored when I speak. My heart burns like fire; it is as though a thousand arrows pierce my flesh.

sentences.zh: 所可惜者，淮西蕩定，河北底寧，承宗斂手削地，韓弘輿疾討賊，豈朝廷之力能制其命哉？

translations.literal: What is regrettable is that Huai Xi has been swept clean and settled, Hebei is settled at the base—Chengzong folded his hands and ceded territory; Han Hong, ill in carriage, attacked the bandit. Was it the court's power that could command their lives?
translations.idiomatic: What grieves me is this: Huai Xi is pacified, Hebei is quieting down, Wang Chengzong has surrendered territory, and Han Hong has taken the field against the rebels while ill. Was it raw imperial force that bent them?

sentences.zh: 直以處置得宜，能服其心耳。

translations.literal: It is simply that the handling was appropriate and able to win their hearts, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: No—it was because the court handled them wisely and won their hearts.

sentences.zh: 陛下建昇平之業，十已八九，何忍還自墮壞，使四方解體乎？」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is establishing the enterprise of ascending peace—it is eight or nine parts in ten. How can you bear to again ruin it yourself and make the four quarters fall apart?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's work of restoring peace is eight or nine tenths complete. How can you bear to wreck it now and let the realm come apart?

sentences.zh: 上以度為朋黨，不之省。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Du a faction member and did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Pei Du as partisan and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 鎛自知不為眾所與，益為巧諂以自固，奏減內外官俸以助國用。

translations.literal: Bo knew himself not supported by the multitude; he all the more practiced artful flattery to secure himself and memorialized to reduce inner and outer officials' salaries to assist state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he lacked public support, Huangfu Bo flattered all the more cleverly to secure his position and proposed cutting the salaries of all officials to help state finances.

sentences.zh: 給事中崔植封還敕書，極論之，乃止。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Cui Zhi sealed and returned the edict, arguing it to the utmost, and then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Cui Zhi returned the edict unopened with a forceful protest, and the proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 植，祐甫之弟子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was Youfu's disciple's son.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhi was a nephew of the former chancellor Cui Youfu.

sentences.zh: 時內出積年繒帛付度支令賣，鎛悉以高價買之，以給邊軍。

translations.literal: At the time the inner palace issued accumulated years' silk and cloth to the Treasury to be sold; Bo entirely bought them at high price and used them to supply border armies.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the palace released years of stored silk for the treasury to sell. Huangfu Bo bought it all at inflated prices and issued it to the frontier armies.

sentences.zh: 其繒帛朽敗，隨手破裂，邊軍聚而焚之。

translations.literal: That silk and cloth was rotten and decayed; at a touch it split apart—the border armies gathered and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: The cloth was rotten and fell apart in their hands. The frontier troops piled it up and burned it.

sentences.zh: 度因奏事言之，鎛於上前引其足曰：「此靴亦內庫所出，臣以錢二千買之，堅完可久服。

translations.literal: Du, while presenting business, spoke of it; Bo before the emperor pulled out his foot and said: "These boots also came from the inner storehouse—I bought them for two thousand cash; firm and whole, they can be worn long.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du raised the matter at audience. Before the emperor Huangfu Bo lifted his foot and said, "These boots also came from the palace stores. I bought them for two thousand cash, and they are sturdy enough to wear for years.

sentences.zh: 度言不可信。」

translations.literal: Du's words cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du's account cannot be trusted.

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 由是鎛益無所憚。

translations.literal: From this Bo all the more had nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Huangfu Bo grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 程異亦自知不合眾心，能廉謹謙遜，為相月餘，不敢知印秉筆，故終免於禍。

translations.literal: Cheng Yi also knew himself not in accord with public sentiment; he was able to be incorrupt, careful, and modest—for more than a month as chancellor he dared not handle the seal and hold the brush, and therefore in the end escaped calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yi knew he lacked public support and kept a low profile—incorrupt, careful, and humble. For more than a month as chancellor he never handled the seal or drafted edicts, and so escaped ruin in the end.

sentences.zh: 五坊使楊朝汶妄捕系人，迫以考捶，責其息錢，遂轉相誣引，所繫近千人。

translations.literal: Five Wards Commissioner Yang Chaowen recklessly arrested and imprisoned people, forced them with examination and beating to demand their interest money, and then in succession falsely implicated one another—those imprisoned nearly reached one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Chaowen, commissioner of the Five Wards, arbitrarily arrested people, tortured them to extract interest payments, and through successive forced confessions implicated nearly a thousand.

sentences.zh: 中丞蕭俛劾奏其狀，裴度、崔群亦以為言。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiao Mian impeached and memorialized the circumstances; Pei Du and Cui Qun also spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Xiao Mian impeached him; Pei Du and Cui Qun raised the case as well.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「姑與卿論用兵事，此小事朕自處之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For now let Us discuss military affairs with you—this small matter I will handle myself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Let us talk of the campaign for now. This petty affair I will settle myself.

sentences.zh: 度曰：「用兵事小，所憂不過山東耳。

translations.literal: Du said: "Using troops is a small matter; what we need worry about is no more than Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du said, "The campaign itself is a minor concern; our real worry is only the situation east of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 五坊使暴橫，恐亂輦轂。」

translations.literal: The Five Wards commissioners are violent and overbearing—I fear they may throw the capital into chaos."
translations.idiomatic: The Five Wards commissioners are brutal and lawless; I fear they will bring disorder to the capital."

sentences.zh: 上不悅，退，召朝汶責之曰：「以汝故，令吾羞見宰相！」

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased. He withdrew, summoned Chaowen, and rebuked him: "Because of you, you have made Us ashamed to face the chancellor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense. After the audience he summoned Yang Chaowen and upbraided him: "Because of you, I am ashamed to face my chancellor!"

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，賜朝汶死，盡釋系者。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Chaowen was sentenced to death and all those imprisoned were released.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Yang Chaowen was ordered to take his own life, and all the detainees were freed.

sentences.zh: 上晚節好神仙，詔天下求方士。

translations.literal: In his later years the emperor came to favor immortals and decreed a search throughout the realm for alchemists.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor grew fond of immortality cults and ordered alchemists sought throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 宗正卿李道古先為鄂岳觀察使，以貪暴聞，恐終獲罪，思所以自媚於上，乃因皇甫鎛薦山人柳泌，雲能合長生藥。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Li Daogu had earlier served as governor of E-Yue; renowned for greed and cruelty, he feared he would ultimately be punished and sought a way to curry favor with the emperor. Through Huangfu Bo he recommended the mountain recluse Liu Bi, saying he could compound an elixir of long life.
translations.idiomatic: Li Daogu, director of the imperial clan, had previously been military governor of E-Yue and was known for greed and brutality. Fearing eventual punishment, he looked for a way to win the emperor's favor and, through Huangfu Bo, recommended the mountaint recluse Liu Bi, claiming he could brew an elixir of immortality.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔泌居興唐觀煉藥。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, an edict ordered Bi to dwell at Xingtang Abbey and refine the medicine.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, the emperor ordered Liu Bi to take up residence at Xingtang Abbey to refine the elixir.

sentences.zh: 十一月，辛巳朔，鹽州奏吐蕃寇河曲、夏州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day xinsi, Yanzhou reported that Tibet raided Hequ and Xiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month (xinsi), Yanzhou reported Tibetan raids on Hequ and Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靈武奏破吐蕃長樂州，克其外城。

translations.literal: Lingwu reported defeating Tibet at Changle Prefecture and capturing its outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu reported a victory over Tibet at Changle Prefecture and the capture of its outer city.

sentences.zh: 柳泌言於上曰：「天台山神仙所聚，多靈草，臣雖知之，力不能致，誠得為彼長吏，庶幾可求。」

translations.literal: Liu Bi said to the emperor: "Tiantai Mountain is where immortals gather; many spirit herbs grow there. Though I know of them, my strength cannot obtain them. If I could truly become magistrate there, perhaps I might seek them."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bi told the emperor, "Tiantai Mountain is where immortals assemble, and spirit herbs abound. I know where they grow, but I lack the means to gather them. If I could serve as prefect there, I might yet obtain them."

sentences.zh: 上信之。

translations.literal: The emperor believed him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以泌權知台州刺史，仍賜服金紫。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Bi was appointed acting prefect of Taizhou and was also granted golden-purple robes.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Liu Bi was made acting prefect of Taizhou and granted the golden-purple insignia of rank.

sentences.zh: 諫官爭論奏，以為：「人主喜方士，未有使之臨民賦政者。」

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials debated and memorialized, holding that: "When a ruler favors alchemists, never yet has one been made to govern the people and administer taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials protested in memorials, arguing, "When sovereigns indulge alchemists, none has ever been set to govern the people and levy taxes."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「煩一州之力而能為人主致長生，臣子亦何愛焉！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If troubling one prefecture's strength can win long life for the ruler, what would subjects begrudge!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "If the labor of one prefecture can win immortality for your ruler, what sacrifice would his servants refuse!"

sentences.zh: 由是群臣莫敢言。

translations.literal: From this none among the ministers dared speak further.
translations.idiomatic: After that no minister dared object.

sentences.zh: 甲午，鹽州奏吐蕃引去。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Yanzhou reported that the Tibetans had withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, Yanzhou reported that the Tibetans had withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以河陽節度使烏重胤為橫海節度使。

translations.literal: On renyin, Heyang military governor Wu Chongyin was made Henghai military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wu Chongyin, military governor of Heyang, was appointed military governor of Henghai.

sentences.zh: 丁未，以華州刺史令狐楚為河陽節度使。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Huazhou governor Linghu Chu was made Heyang military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Linghu Chu, governor of Hua Prefecture, was appointed military governor of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 重胤以河陽精兵三千赴鎮，河陽兵不樂去鄉里，中道潰歸，又不敢入城，屯於城北，將大掠。

translations.literal: Chongyin took three thousand picked Heyang troops to his new command. The Heyang soldiers were unwilling to leave their home districts; midway they broke and fled back. They dared not enter the city and encamped north of the walls, about to plunder on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin set out for his new post with three thousand elite Heyang troops. The soldiers did not want to leave home; they mutinied on the road and straggled back. Too afraid to enter the city, they camped north of the walls and were on the verge of widespread looting.

sentences.zh: 令狐楚適至，單騎出，慰撫之，與俱歸。

translations.literal: Linghu Chu had just arrived; he rode out alone, comforted and reassured them, and returned with them together.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Chu had just arrived. He rode out alone, calmed the men, and led them back into the city.

sentences.zh: 先是，田弘正請自黎陽渡河，會義成節度使李光顏討李師道，裴度曰：「魏博軍既渡河，不可復退，立須進擊，方有成功。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tian Hongzheng had asked to cross the Yellow River from Liyang to join Yicheng military governor Li Guangyan in campaigning against Li Shidao. Pei Du said: "Once the Weibo army has crossed the river it cannot retreat again—it must immediately advance and strike if there is to be success.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tian Hongzheng had proposed crossing the Yellow River at Liyang to join Yicheng governor Li Guangyan against Li Shidao. Pei Du argued, "Once the Weibo army crosses the river it cannot turn back; it must press the attack at once or the campaign will fail.

sentences.zh: 既至滑州，即仰給度支，徒有供餉之勞，更生觀望之勢。

translations.literal: Once they reach Huazhou they will depend on the treasury for supplies—only the toil of provisioning, and a posture of watching and waiting will arise anew.
translations.idiomatic: At Huazhou they would depend on the treasury for rations, gaining nothing but the burden of supply while inviting hesitation and delay.

sentences.zh: 又或與李光顏互相疑阻，益致遷延。

translations.literal: They may also mutually suspect and obstruct Li Guangyan, further causing postponement.
translations.idiomatic: They might also grow suspicious of Li Guangyan and block one another, prolonging the stalemate still further.

sentences.zh: 與其渡河而不進，不若養威於河北。

translations.literal: Rather than cross the river and not advance, better to nurture martial readiness north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Better to build strength north of the river than to cross and then stall.

sentences.zh: 宜且使之秣馬厲兵，俟霜降水落，自楊劉渡河，直指鄆州，得至陽谷置營，則兵勢自盛，賊眾搖心矣。」

translations.literal: For now they should be made to feed horses and sharpen weapons; wait until frost falls and waters subside, then cross from Yangliu, strike straight at Yan Prefecture—if they can reach Yanggu and set camp, military momentum will naturally swell and the rebel host will lose heart."
translations.idiomatic: He should feed his horses, drill his troops, and wait until frost and falling water levels allow a crossing at Yangliu straight toward Yan Prefecture. If he can encamp at Yanggu, our armies will gain momentum and the rebels' morale will crack."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 是月，弘正將魏博全師自楊劉渡河，距鄆州四十里築壘。

translations.literal: That month Hongzheng led the entire Weibo force across from Yangliu, built a fortified camp forty li from Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That month Tian Hongzheng led the full Weibo army across at Yangliu and built a fortified camp forty li from Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 賊中大震。

translations.literal: Within the rebel ranks there was great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through the rebel ranks.

sentences.zh: 功德使上言：「鳳翔法門寺塔有佛指骨，相傳三十年一開，開則歲豐人安。

translations.literal: The Commissioner of Merits and Virtues memorialized: "In the pagoda of Famen Temple at Fengxiang there is a Buddha finger-bone relic; tradition holds it is opened once every thirty years—when opened, the year is abundant and the people secure.
translations.idiomatic: The commissioner of Buddhist merit reported, "Famen Temple's pagoda at Fengxiang holds a Buddha finger-bone relic said to be displayed once every thirty years; when it is opened, harvests are rich and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 來年應開，請迎之。」

translations.literal: Next year it should be opened—We request it be welcomed."
translations.idiomatic: It should be opened next year; we ask that it be brought to court."

sentences.zh: 十二月，庚戌朔，上遣中使帥僧眾迎之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day gengxu, the emperor sent a palace envoy leading monks to welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the first day of the month (gengxu), the emperor dispatched a palace envoy with a monastic escort to fetch the relic.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以春州司戶董重質為試太子詹事，委武寧軍驅使，李愬請之也。

translations.literal: On wuchen, Chunzhou registrar Dong Chongzhi was made provisional grand mentor of the heir apparent and assigned to labor service under the Wujing army—at Li Su's request.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen, Dong Chongzhi, registrar of Chun Prefecture, was made provisional grand mentor of the heir apparent and assigned to the Wujing army for labor duty at Li Su's request.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，魏博、義成軍送所獲李師道都知兵馬使夏侯澄等四十七人，上皆釋弗誅，各付所獲行營驅使，曰：「若有父母欲歸者，優給遣之。

translations.literal: On wuyin, the Weibo and Yicheng armies sent forty-seven captives including Li Shidao's director of military affairs Xiahou Cheng. The emperor released them all without execution and assigned each to labor in the camp that had captured him, saying: "If any have parents who wish to return home, treat them generously and send them off.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Weibo and Yicheng delivered forty-seven captives, including Li Shidao's director of military affairs Xiahou Cheng. The emperor spared them all and assigned each to the camp that had taken him, saying, "If any have parents they wish to rejoin, give them generous travel provisions and send them home.

sentences.zh: 朕所誅者，師道而已。」

translations.literal: Those whom We execute are Shidao alone."
translations.idiomatic: The only man I mean to punish is Shidao himself."

sentences.zh: 於是賊中聞之，降者相繼。

translations.literal: When this was heard within the rebel ranks, surrenderers followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: When word of this reached the rebels, men surrendered in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 初，李文會與兄元規皆在李師古幕下。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Wenhui and his elder brother Yuangui had both served on Li Shigu's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Wenhui and his elder brother Yuangui had both served on Li Shigu's staff.

sentences.zh: 師古薨，師道立，元規辭去，文會屬師道親黨請留。

translations.literal: When Shigu died and Shidao succeeded, Yuangui resigned; Wenhui, through Shidao's close associates, asked to remain.
translations.idiomatic: After Shigu's death, when Shidao took power, Yuangui left service; Wenhui, through Shidao's inner circle, asked to stay on.

sentences.zh: 元規將行，謂文會曰：「我去，身退而安全；

translations.literal: As Yuangui was about to depart he said to Wenhui: "If I go, I withdraw my person and am safe;
translations.idiomatic: As Yuangui prepared to leave he told Wenhui, "If I go, I step back and keep myself safe;

sentences.zh: 汝留，必驟貴而受禍。」

translations.literal: If you stay, you will surely rise suddenly to high rank and suffer disaster."
translations.idiomatic: if you stay, you will soar to power—and then come to ruin."

sentences.zh: 及官軍四臨，平盧兵勢日蹙，將士喧然，皆曰：「高沐、郭日戶、李存為司空忠謀，李文會奸佞，殺沐，囚日戶、存，以致此禍。」

translations.literal: When the imperial armies pressed from all sides and Pinglu's military situation grew daily tighter, officers and soldiers clamored, all saying: "Gao Mu, Guo Rihu, and Li Cun served the grand minister loyally; Li Wenhui is treacherous and corrupt—he killed Mu, imprisoned Rihu and Cun, and brought on this calamity."
translations.idiomatic: As imperial armies closed in from every side and Pinglu's position grew desperate, the troops erupted in uproar: "Gao Mu, Guo Rihu, and Li Cun gave loyal counsel to the grand minister; Li Wenhui is a scheming flatterer. He killed Mu and imprisoned Rihu and Cun—and brought this disaster upon us."

sentences.zh: 師道不得已，出文會攝登州刺史，召日戶、存還幕府。

translations.literal: Shidao, having no choice, sent Wenhui out to serve as acting governor of Deng Prefecture and recalled Rihu and Cun to the headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao had no choice but to transfer Wenhui to acting governor of Deng Prefecture and recall Rihu and Cun to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 上常語宰相：「人臣當力為善，何乃好立朋黨！

translations.literal: The emperor often told the chancellor: "Ministers should strive with all their strength to do good—why do they so love to form factions!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often told his chancellor, "A minister should devote himself to doing good—so why are men so eager to form factions!

sentences.zh: 朕甚惡之。」

translations.literal: We greatly detest it."
translations.idiomatic: I loathe the practice."

sentences.zh: 裴度對曰：「方以類聚，物以群分。

translations.literal: Pei Du replied: "By nature like gathers with like; by kind things flock together.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du answered, "Like natures gather; like kinds flock together.

sentences.zh: 君子、小人志趣同者，勢必相合。

translations.literal: When gentlemen and petty men share the same aims, they are bound to join together.
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen and petty men share the same inclinations, they inevitably band together.

sentences.zh: 君子為徒，謂之同德；

translations.literal: When gentlemen associate, it is called sharing virtue;
translations.idiomatic: When the upright associate, we call it sharing virtue;

sentences.zh: 小人為徒，謂之朋黨；

translations.literal: When petty men associate, it is called forming factions;
translations.idiomatic: when the base associate, we call it forming a faction;

sentences.zh: 外雖相似，內實懸殊，在聖主辯其所為邪正耳。」

translations.literal: Outwardly they may seem alike, but inwardly they are utterly different—the sage ruler has only to discern whether their conduct is crooked or straight.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly alike, inwardly worlds apart. A sage ruler need only judge whether their deeds are righteous or corrupt.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使李愬與平盧兵十一戰，皆捷。

translations.literal: Wujing military governor Li Su fought eleven battles with Pinglu troops and won them all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su, military governor of Wujing, fought eleven engagements against Pinglu forces and won every one.

sentences.zh: 己卯晦，進攻金鄉，克之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, jimao, he advanced and attacked Jinxiang and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month (jimao), he assaulted and took Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 李師道性懦怯，自官軍致討，聞小敗及失城邑，輒憂悸成疾，由是左右皆蔽匿，不以實告。

translations.literal: Li Shidao was by nature timid and cowardly. From the time the imperial armies marched against him, whenever he heard of a small defeat or the loss of a city or district he would fall into anxious dread and illness; because of this those around him all concealed and hid the truth, not telling him what was really happening.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao was timid by nature. After the imperial campaign began, every minor defeat or lost town sent him into panic and illness. His attendants therefore hid the truth and never reported events honestly.

sentences.zh: 金鄉，兗州之要地，既失之，其刺史遣驛騎告急，左右不為通，師道至死竟不知也。

translations.literal: Jinxiang was a strategic place in Yanzhou. Once it was lost, its prefect dispatched a relay rider with an urgent report—but those around Shidao would not pass it through, and to his death Shidao never knew.
translations.idiomatic: Jinxiang was a key strongpoint in Yan Prefecture. When it fell, the prefect sent a courier with an urgent report, but Shidao's attendants blocked it; he died without ever learning of the loss.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝中之下元和十四年（

translations.literal: Middle section, lower part, of the reign of Emperor Xianzong, the Illustrious, Cultured, Martial, Great, Sagely, and Divine Filial Emperor—Yuanhe year 14 (
translations.idiomatic: Middle section, lower part, of the reign of Emperor Xianzong—the Illustrious, Cultured, Martial, Great, Sagely, and Divine Filial Emperor—Yuanhe year 14 (

sentences.zh: 己亥，公元八一九年）

translations.literal: jihai, corresponding to the year 819 CE).
translations.idiomatic: jihai, CE 819).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛已，韓弘拔考城，殺二千餘人。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on xinyi, Han Hong captured Kaocheng and killed more than two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinyi, Han Hong took Kaocheng and killed more than two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，師道所署沐陽令梁洞以縣降於楚州刺史李聽。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Liang Dong, whom Shidao had appointed magistrate of Muyang, surrendered the county to Chuzhou governor Li Ting.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Liang Dong, whom Shidao had installed as magistrate of Muyang, surrendered the county to Li Ting, governor of Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃遣使者論短立藏等來修好，未返，入寇河曲。

translations.literal: Tibet sent envoys including Lun Duanlizang to seek renewed friendship; before they had returned, Tibet raided Hequ.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet sent envoys led by Lun Duanlizang to reopen relations; before they returned home, Tibetan forces raided Hequ.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「其國失信，其使何罪！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Their state broke faith—what crime is there in the envoys!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Their kingdom broke faith—what fault lies with the envoys!"

sentences.zh: 庚寅，遣歸國。

translations.literal: On gengyin, they were sent back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the envoys were sent home unharmed.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，武寧節度使李愬拔魚台。

translations.literal: On renchen, Wujing military governor Li Su captured Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Li Su, military governor of Wujing, captured Yutai.

sentences.zh: 中使迎佛骨至京師，上留禁中三日，乃歷送諸寺，王公士民瞻奉捨施，惟恐弗及，有竭產充施者，有然香臂頂供養者。

translations.literal: When the palace envoy welcoming the Buddha relic reached the capital, the emperor kept it within the forbidden precincts for three days, then had it borne in succession to the various temples. Princes, nobles, officials, and common people venerated it and made offerings, fearing they might not reach it in time; some exhausted their estates to fill the donation bowls, some burned incense on their arms and crowns to worship.
translations.idiomatic: When the relic procession reached Chang'an, the emperor kept the bone in the palace for three days, then sent it from temple to temple. Nobles and commoners thronged to worship and give alms, some bankrupting themselves, others burning incense on their arms and heads in devotion.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎韓愈上表切諫，以為：「佛者，夷狄之一法耳。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Han Yu submitted a memorial urgently remonstrating, holding that: "The Buddha is but one method among the barbarian tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, vice minister of justice, submitted a fierce memorial arguing, "Buddhism is merely a barbarian teaching.

sentences.zh: 自黃帝以至禹，湯、文、武，皆享壽考，百姓安樂，當是時，未有佛也。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor down to Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu—all enjoyed long life, and the hundred surnames were secure and happy; in those times there was as yet no Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor through Yu, Tang, and the kings Wen and Wu, rulers lived long and the people prospered—before Buddhism ever existed.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，始有佛法。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's time Buddhism first appeared.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism first entered China under Emperor Ming of Han.

sentences.zh: 其後亂亡相繼，運祚不長。

translations.literal: After that disorder and ruin followed in succession, and dynastic fortune was not long.
translations.idiomatic: After that, dynasties fell in quick succession and none lasted long.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊、梁、陳、元魏已下，事佛漸謹，年代尤促。

translations.literal: From Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei downward, service to Buddha grew ever more devout, and reigns were especially brief.
translations.idiomatic: From the Liu Song through Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei, emperors grew more pious toward Buddhism—and their reigns grew shorter.

sentences.zh: 惟梁武帝在位四十八年，前後三捨身為寺家奴，竟為侯景所逼，餓死台城，國亦尋滅。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Wu of Liang reigned forty-eight years; thrice before and after he surrendered his body to become a temple slave, yet in the end he was driven by Hou Jing, starved to death at Taicheng, and the state soon perished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liang Wudi reigned forty-eight years, thrice selling himself into temple slavery—yet Hou Jing drove him to starve at Taicheng, and his dynasty soon perished.

sentences.zh: 事佛求福，乃更得禍。

translations.literal: Seeking fortune through serving Buddha, one instead received calamity.
translations.idiomatic: To serve Buddha seeking blessing is to invite disaster.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，佛不足信亦可知矣！

translations.literal: Viewed in this light, that the Buddha is not to be trusted may also be known!
translations.idiomatic: From this it is plain that Buddhism deserves no trust!

sentences.zh: 百姓愚冥，易惑難曉，苟見陛下如此，皆云『天子大聖，猶一心敬信；

translations.literal: The hundred surnames are dull and dark, easy to delude and hard to enlighten; if they see Your Majesty acting thus, all will say, "The Son of Heaven is supremely sage, yet still devotes his whole heart to reverent faith;
translations.idiomatic: The common people are ignorant and easily misled. If they see Your Majesty doing this, they will say, "The Son of Heaven is supremely wise, yet still burns with devotion;

sentences.zh: 百姓微賤，於佛豈可更惜身命。』

translations.literal: We common people, low and mean—how could we spare body and life before the Buddha?"
translations.idiomatic: how can we humble folk cling to our petty lives when the Buddha asks for them?"

sentences.zh: 佛本夷狄之人，口不言先王之法言，身不服先王之法服，不知君臣之義、父子之恩。

translations.literal: The Buddha was originally a man of barbarian tribes; his mouth did not speak the law-words of the former kings, his body did not wear the law-garments of the former kings—he did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister or the grace between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha was a barbarian. He did not speak the sages' words or wear the sages' robes; he knew nothing of the duty between ruler and minister or the love between father and son.

sentences.zh: 假如其身尚在，奉國命來朝京師，陛下容而接之，不過宣政一見，禮賓一設，賜衣一襲，衛而出之於境，不令惑眾也。

translations.literal: Suppose his person were still alive and he came to court at the capital bearing his state's commission—Your Majesty might receive and meet him, but it would be no more than one audience in the Xuanzheng Hall, one banquet in the Ministry of Rites, the gift of one suit of robes, and an escort out of the borders—not allowing him to bewilder the masses.
translations.idiomatic: If he were alive today and came to Chang'an on embassy, Your Majesty might receive him once in Xuanzheng Hall, entertain him once in the Ministry of Rites, grant him a robe, and escort him back across the border—never letting him beguile the people.

sentences.zh: 況其身死已久，枯朽之骨，豈宜以入宮禁！

translations.literal: How much the less should his body long dead, bones withered and rotten, be brought into the palace precincts!
translations.idiomatic: How much less should his dead and rotting bones enter the forbidden palace!

sentences.zh: 古之諸侯得吊於國，尚令巫祝先以桃茢祓除不祥。

translations.literal: When ancient feudal lords received condolences within the state, they still ordered shamans first to drive away ill fortune with peach wands and reed brushes.
translations.idiomatic: When ancient lords received condolences within their domains, they still had shamans purify the way with peach wands and reed brushes.

sentences.zh: 今無故取朽穢之物親視之，巫祝不先，桃茢不用，群臣不言其非，御史不舉其罪，臣實恥之！

translations.literal: Now, without cause, you take a rotten and foul thing and view it in person—no shaman goes first, no peach wand or reed brush is used; the ministers do not speak of its wrong, the censors do not impeach its crime—I am truly ashamed!
translations.idiomatic: Now you handle this filthy relic with your own hands—no purification, no protest from ministers, no impeachment from censors. I am ashamed!

sentences.zh: 乞以此骨會有司，投諸水火，永絕要本，斷天下之疑，絕後代之惑，使天下之人知大聖人之所作為，出於尋常萬萬也，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: I beg that this bone be handed to the proper offices and cast into water and fire, forever cutting off the root of the evil, ending doubt under Heaven and cutting off delusion for later ages—so that all under Heaven may know the acts of the Great Sage are a hundred thousand times beyond the ordinary. Would that not be glorious!
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this bone be given to the proper offices and destroyed by fire and water, uprooting the evil forever, clearing the realm's doubts, and showing that a true sage's conduct rises immeasurably above the common run. Would that not be magnificent!

sentences.zh: 佛如有靈，能作禍福，凡有殃咎，宜加臣身。」

translations.literal: If the Buddha has spirit and can bring calamity or blessing, let any misfortune fall on my person alone.
translations.idiomatic: If Buddha has power to bless or curse, let every curse fall on me alone.

sentences.zh: 上得表，大怒，出示宰相，將加愈極刑。

translations.literal: When the emperor received the memorial he was greatly enraged; he showed it to the chancellor and was about to impose the extreme penalty on Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and flew into a rage. He showed it to his chancellor and was ready to execute Han Yu.

sentences.zh: 裴度、崔群為言：「愈雖狂，發於忠懇，宜寬容以開言路。」

translations.literal: Pei Du and Cui Qun spoke on his behalf: "Though Yu is wild, his words spring from loyal earnestness—it is fitting to show forbearance and open the path of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du and Cui Qun pleaded for him: "Han Yu may be reckless, but he spoke from loyal conviction. Forbearance will keep the road of honest counsel open."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，貶愈為潮州刺史。

translations.literal: On guisi, Yu was demoted to governor of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Han Yu was demoted to governor of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 自戰國之世，老、莊與儒者爭衡，更相是非。

translations.literal: From the Warring States age, Laozi and Zhuangzi contended with the Confucians, each in turn condemning the other.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Warring States period, Daoists and Confucians have quarreled, each denouncing the other.

sentences.zh: 至漢末，益之以佛，然好者尚寡。

translations.literal: By late Han Buddhism was added, yet those who favored it were still few.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Han, Buddhism had joined the dispute, but its followers were still few.

sentences.zh: 晉、宋以來，日益繁熾，自帝王至於士民，莫不尊信。

translations.literal: From Jin and Song onward it grew daily more flourishing—from emperors down to common scholars and people, none did not honor and believe it.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin and Song dynasties onward it spread until emperors and commoners alike revered it.

sentences.zh: 下者畏慕罪福，高者論難空有。

translations.literal: The lowly feared and admired retribution and reward; the lofty debated emptiness and existence.
translations.idiomatic: The humble feared karma; the learned debated emptiness and being.

sentences.zh: 獨愈惡其蠹財惑眾，力排之，其言多矯激太過。

translations.literal: Only Yu detested its draining wealth and bewitching the masses, and strove to repel it—yet his words were mostly overwrought and excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu alone hated Buddhism for wasting wealth and beguiling the people, and fought it with fierce rhetoric that often overshot the mark.

sentences.zh: 惟《送文暢師序》最得其要，曰：「夫鳥俯而啄，仰而四顧，獸深居而簡出，懼物之為己害也，猶且不免焉。

translations.literal: Only his "Preface on Seeing Off Master Wenchang" most hits the mark, saying: "Birds bow their heads to peck, then lift them and look all around; beasts dwell deep and come out sparingly, fearing that things may harm them—yet even so they cannot escape.
translations.idiomatic: Only his Preface on Sending Off the Monk Wenchang strikes the true note: "Birds peck with heads bowed, then look about; beasts hide deep and venture out warily, fearing harm—yet even they cannot always escape.

sentences.zh: 弱之肉，強之食。

translations.literal: The flesh of the weak is food for the strong.
translations.idiomatic: The weak are meat for the strong.

sentences.zh: 今吾與文暢安居而暇食，優遊以生死，與禽獸異者，寧可不知其所自邪！」

translations.literal: Now you and I, Wenchang, dwell at ease and eat in leisure, roaming freely between life and death—how can we differ from birds and beasts yet not know whence this comes!
translations.idiomatic: You and I, Wenchang, live at ease and eat at leisure, drifting through life and death unlike the beasts—can we not ask where our comfort comes from?"

sentences.zh: 丙申，田弘正奏敗淄青兵於東阿，殺萬餘人。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Tian Hongzheng memorialized defeating Ziqing troops at Dong'e and killing more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Tian Hongzheng reported defeating Ziqing forces at Dong'e with more than ten thousand killed.

sentences.zh: 滄州刺史李宗奭與橫海節度使鄭權不葉，不受其節制，權奏之。

translations.literal: Cangzhou governor Li Zongshi was at odds with Henghai military governor Zheng Quan and would not accept his command; Quan memorialized this.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongshi, governor of Cang Prefecture, clashed with Henghai governor Zheng Quan and refused his orders; Quan reported him to court.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使追之，宗奭使其軍中留己，表稱懼亂未敢離州。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to summon him. Zongshi had his army detain him; he submitted a memorial saying he feared unrest and dared not leave the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent a palace envoy to fetch him. Zongshi had his troops hold the envoy and memorialized that unrest made it unsafe to leave his post.

sentences.zh: 詔以烏重胤代權，將吏懼，逐宗奭。

translations.literal: An edict made Wu Chongyin replace Quan; officers and clerks grew afraid and drove Zongshi out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replaced Quan with Wu Chongyin; Zongshi's subordinates, alarmed, expelled him.

sentences.zh: 宗奭奔京師，辛丑，斬於獨柳之下。

translations.literal: Zongshi fled to the capital; on xinchou he was beheaded beneath the Lone Willow.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongshi fled to Chang'an and on xinchou was beheaded at Lone Willow Tree.

sentences.zh: 丙午，田弘正奏敗平盧兵於陽谷。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Tian Hongzheng memorialized defeating Pinglu troops at Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Tian Hongzheng reported a victory over Pinglu forces at Yanggu.

sentences.zh: CATEGORY:資治通鑑

translations.literal: CATEGORY: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
